title: CDI - Senior Context & Analytics Engineer - Paris
descriptionHtml:
Mission

Un agent ne vaut que ce que valent les données et les connaissances sur lesquelles il répond. Pipelines, modèles de données, définitions de métriques, droits d’accès : vous créez et gouvernez ce socle, et les applications et les agents de nos clients s’appuient dessus. Quand un analyste ou un agent demande un chiffre, la réponse est celle de l’équipe finance, accompagnée de sa définition et de sa source.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que les métiers et les agents puissent se fier aux données, et les utilisent.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Context & Analytics Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités

Avec les équipes métier et les analystes, il s’agit de définir ce que signifie chaque métrique et de vérifier que les données y correspondent. Sur ce socle, les Product Engineers et les AI Engineers construisent applications et agents.

Les Platform Engineers exploitent l’infrastructure sur laquelle tournent vos pipelines. Les échanges avec les data owners et les équipes de gouvernance du client, la relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues complètent le quotidien.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des pipelines d’ingestion et des modèles de données, avec dbt par exemple.
  • Mettre en place des contrôles de qualité des données et maintenir le lineage.
  • Construire la couche sémantique et les définitions de métriques, pour que les personnes et les agents utilisent les mêmes chiffres, y compris en text-to-SQL.
  • Définir les règles de gouvernance et les droits d’accès.
  • Construire des pipelines de connaissances pour le RAG : indexation, chunking, métadonnées, permissions.
  • Préparer le contexte exploitable par les agents : métadonnées, définitions, lineage et permissions.

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous écrivez du SQL avec aisance et modélisez les données pour l’analyse.
  2. Des pipelines de données planifiés, testés et surveillés figurent à votre actif.
  3. Aux côtés des équipes métier, vous définissez les métriques et vérifiez que les données veulent bien dire ce que tout le monde croit y lire.
  4. La qualité des données, la documentation et les droits d’accès comptent pour vous.
  5. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Python pour le traitement de données.
  • Une plateforme de données cloud, comme BigQuery, Snowflake ou Databricks.
  • Une couche sémantique ou un metrics store.
  • La préparation de documents pour le RAG : chunking, indexation, métadonnées.
  • Des outils de data catalogue ou de lineage.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Dans un métier où deux tableaux de bord affichent parfois deux chiffres différents, ce poste consiste à rétablir la confiance : un chiffre juste, une définition partagée, une source identifiable. Ce travail, discret quand il réussit, conditionne tout ce que les autres archétypes construisent au-dessus.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets, avec les AI Engineers et l’appui de la communauté Context & Analytics Engineer, notamment le context engineering, c’est-à-dire le travail qui rend les données exploitables par les agents d’IA. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Context & Analytics Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme les chapters AI Architect et AI Product Manager.

Processus de recrutement

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

  1. Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

  5. Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.
  6. Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

title: Clinical AI Research Lead
descriptionHtml:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

Heidi is building AI that works at the frontier of clinical practice. As we pursue medical device registration and expand our clinical trial portfolio and product portfolio, we need someone who can hold the full arc from regulatory strategy to research protocol to working prototypes and translate across all of them.

This role is designed for a rare profile: clinically trained, technically capable, and research-rigorous. You will own the innovation pipeline from problem identification through validated prototype, coordinate the company's clinical research programme, and serve as the internal bridge between product, regulation, and evidence. You will operate as a senior individual contributor with a small specialist team and broad cross-functional mandate.

 

What you’ll do

Research & Evidence Programme

  • Lead and support clinical trials and pilots adjacent to product development and regulation from protocol through analysis and dissemination

  • Design evaluations with research/publication-grade rigour: statistical power, confounder control, reproducible methodology

  • Provide analytical support company-wide - elevating ad hoc analysis to defensible evidence

Regulatory & Compliance Intelligence

  • Translate evolving UK and international medical device regulation into actionable product and development constraints

  • Generate and maintain technical documentation, clinical evaluation reports, and post-market surveillance artefacts - directly analytically supporting the regulatory team.

  • Partner with compliance to ensure regulatory soundness is built in, not bolted on, a strategic moat, not a checklist

  • Serve as the accessible regulatory resource for product, engineering, models and commercial teams: making regulation legible, usable and deeply embedded into all engineering practices.

  • This role is strategic support, and ownership of all product and regulatory adjacent research activities with a strong supporting team to drive progress and delivery.

Cross-functional AI & Research Support

  • Act as a senior research partner to product squads, commercial teams, and leadership, providing evidence, framing decisions, and raising analytical standards

  • Supporting commercial requests with tender applications etc…

 

What you'll need

Clinical

  • Qualified clinician with active understanding of clinical workflow, risk, and patient safety

  • Experience in medical device or clinical AI evaluation, including familiarity with MHRA, UKCA, and/or EU MDR frameworks

Research

  • Postgraduate research training in a relevant field (clinical informatics, AI/ML, health data science, or similar)

  • Demonstrated ability to design, execute, and disseminate clinical or applied research independently

  • Fluency in quantitative methods: statistical modelling, NLP evaluation, speech analytics, and performance benchmarking

  • Skills in implementation science and translational projects involving new technologies

Leadership & Communication

  • Strong written communication, capable of producing high-quality documentation for clinical, regulatory, and commercial audiences

  • Collaborative operator in a fast-moving environment; able to work across seniority levels and functions

  • Experience managing small teams or contractors; structured, outcome-oriented

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

 

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

We take care of you.

We offer 25 days of paid time off per year, 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder, a €100/month Healthy Heidi's wellness stipend, a €500 home office budget, a €700 annual learning and development budget, 26 weeks paid primary parental leave and 18 weeks paid secondary parental leave, fertility support up to €7,000, up to four weeks of work from anywhere per year, Recharge Days after major milestones and busy periods, 10 days per year of clinical leave for eligible clinical roles, and a hybrid working environment with 3 days in the office.

We chose to open-source our benefits hub, if you care to take a peek.

Heidi’s commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

Heidi is dedicated to creating an equitable, inclusive, and supportive work environment that brings people together from diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Our strength is in our differences. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are proud to welcome all applicants as we're committed to promoting a culture of opportunity for all.

  • Proficiency in ISO/G-code and/or conversational programming.

  • Ability to read engineering drawings and interpret dimensional tolerances, geometric tolerances, and surface finish requirements.

  • Experience machining stainless steel, aluminium, titanium, or nickel-based alloys.

  • Confidence using precision measuring instruments and checking your own work.

Vos missions

Pourquoi vous allez adorer travailler avec nous ?

title: Commercial Partnerships & Events Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Adclear

At Adclear, we're building the trust layer for how the world's most regulated companies bring products to market. Every bank, lender and investment platform runs into the same invisible pain: compliance review that slows down every campaign, every launch, every idea. We're turning the function that has always said 'no' into infrastructure that says 'yes, and here's how'.

Founded in 2024, we already work with leading innovators and established enterprises including Monzo, Lloyds, PensionBee, Kraken and Coinbase. We've raised 2.6m and we're scaling fast. Now we need someone to take our name into the rooms where our buyers are, and turn those rooms into pipeline.

The role

Field marketing and partnerships are two of the biggest levers in how Adclear goes to market. Our breakfasts, dinners and panels are where compliance and marketing leaders from banks, lenders and fintechs meet us, meet each other, and see what modern compliance looks like. Our partnerships with compliance bodies, industry voices and marketing institutions carry our name into conversations we're not yet part of.

This role owns both, and is measured on what they produce commercially: the right people in the room, warm conversations handed to sales, and opportunities in the pipeline. Running a great event matters, but it's the starting point, not the job.

We run around three events a quarter. You'll decide who we need to reach, build the event or partnership that gets us in front of them, fill it, work the room, and make sure the conversations turn into meetings.

This is an early-stage seat. You'll be a team of one on this, working directly with the founders and commercial team, and you'll pick up whatever it takes to make go-to-market work, even when it isn't strictly on the brief. Have a look at our LinkedIn and socials to see what we already do, then imagine what you'd do with it.

What you'll do

Field marketing

  • Own the field marketing calendar: around three events a quarter across breakfasts, dinners and panels, plus third-party events and conferences where our buyers already gather.

  • Start from the pipeline, not the venue: agree with the founders and sales which accounts and personas each event is for, and design the theme and format to land with them.

  • Fill the room with the right people. Build target lists with sales, invite personally, chase RSVPs and find another way in when the first one doesn't work.

  • Work the room on the day: make introductions, spot buying signals and connect guests with the right person at Adclear.

  • Turn conversations into meetings: run follow-up with sales, so every event produces booked calls and new opportunities.

  • Get the event done well: venue, speakers, run of show, suppliers and budget, without letting logistics become the job.

  • Create the assets yourself where it's quicker: invites, event graphics and social posts.

Partnerships

  • Own relationships with compliance bodies, industry influencers and marketing institutions, from first outreach to co-hosted events, joint content and referrals.

  • Prioritise partners by commercial value: who gives us access to the buyers and accounts we want.

  • Spot and pitch new partnership opportunities, and negotiate what each side gets out of it.

Commercial impact

  • Track what each event and partnership produces: who came, meetings booked, pipeline created, deals influenced.

  • Report back to the founders and use the numbers to decide what we do more of, change, or stop.

  • Pitch in across go-to-market wherever you can add value, from campaigns to content to sales support.

What we're looking for

  • Startup or scale-up experience. You've worked in a small, fast-moving team where you wore several hats and got things done without a big budget or a support team behind you.

  • Commercial instinct. You think in terms of accounts, pipeline and outcomes. You know the difference between a full room and a room full of buyers, and you care about the second.

  • Hustle. You don't wait for RSVPs to arrive. You chase, follow up, and find another way in.

  • Confident with senior people. You're comfortable walking up to a Head of Compliance at a bank, starting a real conversation, and making the right introduction.

  • You can plan an event, write the invite, design the graphic, negotiate with a partner and update the CRM, sometimes all in the same day.

  • Organised under pressure. There's always one event being planned, one being filled and one being followed up. You keep them all moving.

  • Ownership. You treat every event and partnership as yours, including the results.

How we work

  • London, 4 days a week in our Farringdon office.

  • Founders are closely involved day to day, and you'll work directly with them and the commercial team.

  • You own your events and partnerships from day one, including the results.

  • Your wins will be visible and celebrated across the company and the market.

  • This isn't the right role if you want a fixed lane or a strict 40-hour week. Events mean the occasional early breakfast and late dinner.

Compensation

  • Competitive salary

  • Meaningful equity

  • Private healthcare and dental

  • Hardware budget

  • Monthly gym contribution

  • Professional development budget

title: Community Manager
descriptionHtml:
You make sure fellows are well, feel part of a community, and get help quickly when something goes wrong.

  • Salary: £86,750–£121,500 per year. We may be able to pay more for exceptional candidates.

  • Location: London, at our office at LISA

  • Hours: 0.5 to 1 full-time equivalent

  • Visa: We can sponsor a Skilled Worker visa, but approval isn't guaranteed.

Why work at Pivotal

Pivotal finds people who can work on the biggest risks from advanced AI and gets them working on them. Since 2024, 135 fellows have taken part in our fellowships, and alumni now work at METR, Apollo Research, UK AISI and GovAI. We have grown from 2 staff in 2024 to 10 today, and we plan to reach at least 16 in 2027. Read more about us at pivotal-research.org, and about what it is like to work here.

What you will own

You’ll own the health of our community. You support fellows in doing better physically, mentally and socially. By the end of 2027, we may have more than 70 fellows on site at once.

Most of your work is going to be preventive. You find fellows who need support early, support Research Managers to give good day-to-day pastoral care, and make sure each cohort has a good social life. When something serious happens, such as a wellbeing crisis or a conflict, you are the person Research Managers and fellows turn to. That part of the role needs good judgement, discretion and an ability to handle sensitive situations well.

  • Escalation point. Be the person Research Managers and fellows go to for serious wellbeing or conflict issues, as set out in our community health policy.

  • Early support. Run short check-ins or a survey before each cohort starts, to find fellows who need support early.

  • Policies and training. Keep our community health and conduct policies current, and train Research Managers to give day-to-day pastoral support.

  • Community life. Make sure each cohort has a good social life, for example through fellow social leads with a small budget, and work with the Fellowships Generalist on events.

  • Wellbeing across programs. Track wellbeing across cohorts and propose changes to program design.

Who does well in this role

  • Experience in community health, pastoral care, HR or a similar role.

  • Good judgement and discretion with sensitive information.

  • You stay calm in difficult situations, and you keep clear boundaries.

  • You care about reducing catastrophic risks.

We don’t expect anyone to be strong in all of this. If the role excites you, please apply, even if you match only part of what we describe here.

How we hire

We review applications as they come in, so applying early helps. The process has these stages:

  • Written application. A short form and your CV. It takes about 30 minutes.

  • Automated video interview. About 10 minutes. You record short answers to a few questions, at a time that suits you.

  • Work task. About 2 hours, based on real work in this role. We pay you for this time. You may use AI tools, as you would in the job. Tell us which ones you used and how.

  • Personal interview. About 45 minutes. We discuss your work task and how you would approach the role. With your consent, we record it so that more of the team can review it.

  • Work trial and references. Up to three paid days working with us at our office in London. We also speak to two referees, after asking you.

If you need an adjustment at any stage, such as extra time, tell us and we will arrange it. If you have questions, email ----- £86,750 – £121,500

title: Compliance Officer / MLRO Switzerland & Liechtenstein
descriptionHtml:
Compliance Officer / MLRO - Switzerland & Liechtenstein

 

About Keyrock

 

Since 2017, Keyrock has been a change-maker in digital assets. We're a global, remote-first team of 180+ people across 40+ nationalities, with hubs in Brussels, London, Paris, New York and Chicago.

We provide liquidity across 80+ centralized and decentralized exchanges - a position cemented by our Series C, led by SC Ventures. Today we run a full spectrum of capital markets businesses across centralized and on-chain venues: market making, high-frequency trading, options, OTC, DeFi trading desks, advisory, and asset management.

We're building toward the agentic investment banking capabilities for the era of digital finance. A proprietary agentic layer runs the mechanics of the market, so our people can focus on the work code cannot do: the deal, the relationship, and the judgement.

 

We're not just envisioning the future of finance - we're building it.

 

Mission statement

We are looking for an experienced and driven Compliance Officer and MLRO for our Switzerland and Liechtenstein based entities. You will join a dynamic and dedicated Group Compliance team, operating as a key member while focusing primarily on our Switzerland and Liechtenstein operational entities. This role offers an exciting opportunity to make a wider impact across the organization by working on broader, group-level projects, allowing you to contribute to the global compliance framework and help grow the group as a whole.

 

Job description

 

  • Ensuring compliance with all relevant laws and regulations applicable to Switzerland and Liechtenstein by developing and implementing the policies and procedures ;

  • Conducting compliance risk assessments and elaborating an annual compliance plan;

  • Developing and implementing a plan of second-line controls and conducting the tests;

  • Assessing future business activities to identify potential compliance risks;

  • Ensuring the firm’s policies and procedures are being communicated effectively to all relevant employees;

  • Ensuring the compliance trainings are effective and up to date;

  • Keeping abreast with regulatory changes and maintaining the policies and procedures up to date;

  • Collaborate with internal departments such as Trading Operations, Finance, Risk management, IT & Security, etc… to integrate compliance requirements into business processes.

  • Being responsible for oversight of Keyrock CH and LI compliance with its AML obligations and acting as a focal point for the firm’s AML activity (MLRO).

  • Carrying out the duties of a MLRO as per the AML/CTF Framework

  • Representing Keyrock CH and LI in all matters of money laundering prevention internally and externally;

  • Serving as a subject matter expert on AML/CTF matters, providing guidance and support to the compliance team and other departments;

  • Conducting regular audits and reviews to ensure compliance with AML/CTF requirements and internal policies

  • Drafting of compliance points of attention and recommendations and assisting the Group Head of Compliance or Group General Counsel (Group level) with management information reports;

 

Background and experience

  • Solid experience as a Compliance officer (2nd line of defense) in a regulated financial institution in Switzerland and/or Liechtenstein, ideally with exposure to MLRO responsibilities or similar

  • Experience in engaging with Swiss and Liechtenstein regulatory authorities;

  • Excellent knowledge of financial regulations such as MiCAR, AML/CTF, market abuse , data privacy;

  • Understanding of the digital assets ecosystem is a major plus;

  • A relevant degree, preferably in business or law, is required;

  • Extensive experience in implementation of monitoring and control processes to support policies and procedures;

  • A compliance qualification for example ACAMS or a Masters in a related field would be an advantage;

 

Our recruitment philosophy

We look for self-aware candidates who bring both the core skills required for the role and a deep alignment with our performance principles. We seek fiercely passionate, mission-driven people who communicate with purpose and practice proactive ownership. The perfect fit? A crypto enthusiast who prioritizes mission over ego, maintains a commercial mindset, and delivers long-term value through pragmatic flexibility.

Our offer

 

  • A competitive salary and benefits package

  • Annual Team Retreats: a yearly offsite dedicated to strategy, celebration of our wins and fun team activities

  • Opportunity to work remotely

  • Fast-paced, highly intellectually stimulating working environment

  • The freedom to create your own entrepreneurial experience by being part of a team of people in search of excellence

 

As an employer we are committed to building a positive and collaborative work environment. We welcome employees of all backgrounds, and hire, reward and promote entirely based on merit and performance.

 

Due to the nature of our business and external requirements, we perform background checks on all potential employees, passing which is a prerequisite to join Keyrock.

About Aphex

We're the construction coordination platform that's replacing outdated spreadsheets with multiplayer tools that delivery teams love. Major contractors like BAM, Balfour Beatty, SKANSKA, Kier, MACE, and Murphy use Aphex to deliver their projects ranging from £50 million to multi-billion pound mega projects.

We're tackling an industry that drives 10% of global GDP yet has seen productivity decline for 20 years. It's time for change.

 

The Role

As a Customer Success Associate at Aphex, you'll learn our Land & Expand Engine inside one of the highest-paced teams at the company: the UK Customer Success Hub.

Your job is to help major contractors get genuine value out of Aphex on their live projects. You'll be in the room and on site with planners, engineers, construction managers, and project directors, helping them embed weekly planning routines, daily coordination, and the reporting that makes their projects run better.

This is a fast progression role. You'll start in apprentice mode alongside the UK CS team, learning the playbook by doing it. Within 6 to 9 months, most CSAs are running their own portfolio of projects as full Customer Success Managers. We hire people who are hungry for that progression and ready to earn it from day one, not waiting until month nine.

title: Data Engineer - 3 Months Contract
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an experienced Senior Data Engineer with a strong background in designing, deploying, configuring, and managing enterprise-scale data engineering platforms within secure, on-premises and air-gapped environments.

The ideal candidate will have extensive hands-on experience working with Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark clusters, including installation, configuration, administration, troubleshooting, performance optimisation, and workload management in environments with restricted or no internet connectivity.

This role will support our Global Data Centre (GDC) environment, requiring a candidate who understands the operational and technical challenges of delivering robust, scalable, and secure data platforms within isolated infrastructure.

The successful candidate will work closely with infrastructure, platform, DevOps, and data engineering teams to build and maintain reliable data processing capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, deploy, configure, and maintain Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark clusters in on-premises and air-gapped environments.
  • Manage the full lifecycle of Hadoop/Spark platforms, including installation, upgrades, patching, configuration, monitoring, and troubleshooting.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain scalable data pipelines for batch and distributed data processing.
  • Optimise Spark workloads and Hadoop cluster performance, including resource allocation, job scheduling, and capacity management.
  • Work with PostgreSQL and other enterprise data systems to support data integration, storage, and processing requirements.
  • Support the deployment and management of containerised applications using Kubernetes and Helm.
  • Implement and manage service-to-service communication and traffic management using Istio Service Mesh.
  • Ensure software dependencies, container images, packages, and platform components can be deployed and maintained without external internet connectivity.
  • Implement secure configuration and operational practices aligned with enterprise security requirements.
  • Troubleshoot complex infrastructure, cluster, application, and data pipeline issues.
  • Collaborate with infrastructure, security, DevOps, and application teams to ensure platform stability and availability.
  • Maintain technical documentation, deployment procedures, operational runbooks, and platform architecture documentation.
  • Support integration with legacy enterprise data systems, including VSAM.

Requirements

Required Technical Skills & Experience

1. Apache Hadoop & Apache Spark

  • Strong hands-on experience deploying, configuring, and administering Apache Hadoop clusters.
  • Proven experience deploying and managing Apache Spark clusters and workloads.
  • Experience with distributed data processing, batch processing, and large-scale data pipelines.
  • Strong understanding of cluster architecture, resource management, performance tuning, and troubleshooting.
  • Experience operating big data platforms in on-premises and air-gapped environments.

2. Air-Gapped & On-Premises Infrastructure

  • Practical experience working in isolated, restricted-network, or air-gapped environments.
  • Understanding of offline software installation, dependency management, package repositories, and container image management.
  • Experience managing platform deployments without direct access to public internet repositories.
  • Knowledge of secure infrastructure operations and enterprise deployment standards.

3. Containerisation & Platform Engineering

  • Experience with Kubernetes-based platform deployments.
  • Hands-on experience with Helm charts for application and platform deployments.
  • Working knowledge of Istio Service Mesh, including traffic management, service discovery, and secure service-to-service communication.
  • Understanding of container orchestration and microservices architecture.

4. Data Systems & Engineering

  • Strong experience with PostgreSQL, including database integration and performance considerations.
  • Experience designing, developing, and maintaining data pipelines.
  • Understanding of distributed data storage and processing architectures.
  • Knowledge of VSAM and integration with legacy enterprise data environments.

Preferred / Desirable Skills

  • Experience supporting large-scale enterprise or government data centre environments.
  • Familiarity with Linux system administration.
  • Experience with infrastructure automation and configuration management.
  • Knowledge of data security, access controls, encryption, and secure data handling.
  • Experience with monitoring, logging, and platform observability.
  • Exposure to DevOps and CI/CD practices in restricted-network environments.

Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate will be a hands-on technical engineer rather than purely an architectural or theoretical resource. They should be comfortable taking ownership of the deployment, administration, troubleshooting, and ongoing operational management of Hadoop and Spark platforms.

Candidates must be able to demonstrate practical experience working within environments where internet connectivity is restricted or unavailable, with an understanding of the additional complexities involved in deploying and maintaining enterprise data platforms in such environments.

title: Data Scientist, Data Quality & Provenance
descriptionHtml:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

📊 About our Data Quality & Provenance Team

Our Data Quality & Provenance team sits within Wayve’s AI Platform organisation and builds the evidence that helps teams make confident decisions about the data underpinning our embodied AI systems. We develop statistically robust methods, metrics and tools to determine when data-quality, annotation and evaluation signals can be trusted—and when they cannot.

🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Define measurable, statistically rigorous concepts of data quality, including coverage, label quality, uncertainty, provenance and model performance.

  • Apply statistical-inference methods to multi-rater annotation, label ambiguity, dataset coverage and black-box model evaluation.

  • Partner with annotation, autonomy and evaluation teams to translate practical quality questions into defensible metrics.

  • Build automated reports that clearly communicate confidence, limitations and appropriate interpretation.

  • Analyse large annotation datasets using Python and SQL to identify quality issues and inform decisions.

  • Iterate on metrics and reporting based on feedback from the teams using them.

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • Statistical methods for distinguishing genuine data-quality problems from label ambiguity, inconsistent annotation or evaluation noise.

  • Labeler and dataset metrics that support training-data selection, simulation, annotation acceptance and model evaluation.

  • Reusable quality artefacts that replace one-off analyses with registered, automated metrics and reports.

  • Multi-rater and human-in-the-loop ML systems, including approaches such as Dawid–Skene-style models, psychometrics and inter-rater agreement.

  • Quality standards spanning coverage, uncertainty, provenance, annotation quality and predictive-model performance.

  • Integration of data-science outputs into the platform workflows used by engineering and research teams

🙌 You should apply if

  • You have strong foundations in classical statistics, including experimental design, sampling, modelling, estimation and inference.

  • You have practical experience with rater or annotator modelling, inter-rater agreement, label uncertainty or related methods.

  • You understand data quality across dimensions such as coverage, label quality, uncertainty, provenance and model performance.

  • You have worked with annotation tooling, QA methodologies, human-in-the-loop ML systems or multi-rater labelled datasets.

  • You have strong Python and SQL skills and are confident analysing large, complex datasets.

  • You can turn ambiguous stakeholder questions into rigorous, usable metrics and clearly communicate uncertainty, limitations and decision implications.

  • Experience with probabilistic or Bayesian modelling, production platform integrations or safety-critical data would be an advantage.


🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

🔍 The Interview Process

Our process is clear and respectful of your time

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

title: Data Scientist – Optimization & Control
descriptionHtml:
Role

You’ll improve and extend the decision logic behind our battery fleet. Our optimization already runs our batteries every day; now we want to make it sharper, more robust and ready for new use cases. Our batteries sit behind the meter at industrial sites, so every decision has to balance customer savings, grid constraints and market value under uncertainty. Our data scientists and quantitative researchers work as one team and often across each other's topics.

 

What you will do

The role covers two closely linked areas. You can work in either one and switch between them as priorities and your interests evolve:

  • Fleet optimization: Plan how each battery runs over the coming hours and days, combining customer savings, grid fee rules and market value within each site's limits. Forecasts of load, PV and prices are generated and fed into the plan, which has to stay robust to their uncertainty. You also measure how much value we actually capture.

  • On-site control: Make the plan work in reality. Within our local control system, you design the logic that executes the schedule at each site, reacts to deviations and falls back safely when data or devices fail, while hard limits such as grid capacity, feed-in restrictions and state of charge always hold.

 

Topics you'll work on

You join work that is already running and take ownership of topics as priorities require. These are the areas where we want to add strength:

  • Improving and extending our optimization models for sequential decision-making on time series, across customer savings, grid fee rules and market value.

  • Making decisions more robust to forecast uncertainty (load, PV, prices).

  • Developing the on-site decision logic of our local control system: MPC, constraint handling and fallbacks.

  • Making sure hard constraints always hold in operation: grid connection limits, feed-in restrictions, state of charge.

  • Analyzing where we lose value compared to what was possible, and simulating new use cases before go-live.

  • Bringing models into production together with our engineers.

 

What we are looking for

  • Strong in optimization or control under uncertainty, e.g. LP/MILP, MPC, stochastic or robust optimization, state estimation or Kalman filtering.

  • Experience with, or at least exposure to, predictive modeling and machine learning, or a strong background in statistics.

  • Good Python skills and the ambition to write clean code that runs in production, not just in notebooks. You don't need to be a software engineer by training, but you care about code quality and use AI tools to move fast.

  • You are comfortable with messy real-world time-series data and team up with our data engineers to clean and prepare it for modeling.

  • You think in constraints and failure cases and make pragmatic decisions without perfect requirements.

  • You enjoy working closely in a small team, learning each other's topics and covering for each other.

  • Nice to have: battery storage, microgrids or energy management; using probabilistic forecasts in decision-making; German energy markets and regulation.

 

What it means to work at BEO

  • We are a small team taking on a hard problem, and we hold ourselves to a high bar. We value ownership, direct and honest communication, and getting better every day. If you like solving complex problems, you'll fit right in.

  • Our office is in central Munich. We offer plenty of flexibility but ask for an office-first commitment. People learn faster and get more done together.

  • We offer a competitive salary, equity upside in the company, and top-notch equipment (you choose what you need).

  • You'll join us early in our journey. The foundations are in place, but it's still essentially day one, with plenty of opportunity to shape how we tackle one of the most significant challenges of our time.

 

Next steps

We move fast. Most processes are completed within 2 weeks. Apply if this sounds like you.

title: Deine Ausbildung: Fachinformatiker (m/w/d) für Systemintegration
descriptionHtml:

Bei der Deutschen Extrakt Kaffee GmbH (DEK) dreht sich vieles um Kaffee. Damit unsere Kolleginnen und Kollegen jeden Tag ihre Arbeit machen können, braucht es im Hintergrund aber auch eine zuverlässige IT. Und genau hier kommst du ins Spiel.

descriptionHtml:
Who we are

Most organizations understand the potential of AI, but struggle to translate that ambition into real operational change. The challenge is rarely the technology itself. It is how AI fits into complex systems, workflows, and engineering organizations that have evolved over years. We believe AI transformation cannot be designed purely in strategy documents. The real strategy only emerges by building, deploying, and operating AI systems inside the organization.

That’s why we work directly with enterprise IT and software teams to design and implement AI systems in real environments. This includes enabling engineering organizations to work in fundamentally new ways by introducing AI-native development practices, frameworks, and technical assets that change how teams build and operate software. It also includes building custom AI systems that unblock difficult modernization or harmonization efforts where traditional approaches have stalled.

Our team has a strong track record of building high-impact AI systems and scaling engineering teams inside complex enterprises. If you enjoy solving hard enterprise problems and turning ambitious ideas into systems that actually run in production, you’ll feel at home at supermodular.ai.

Your role

supermodular.ai operates through three core roles: AI Strategy, Deployment Strategy and Forward Deployed Engineering.

As a Deployment Strategist, you are responsible for translating AI strategy into a live enterprise engagement. You own delivery inside the account, including stakeholder management, prioritization, execution and the initiatives we commit to next.

You work directly with enterprise leaders, engineers and operators to understand how their systems and workflows function today, identify where AI can create meaningful operational impact and shape initiatives that can realistically be deployed inside the organization.

title: Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Since early 2024, we've gone from 0 to over 900 customers, succeeding where many have tried and failed before. We have a big mission: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run and grow a renewables installation business, and through that to make a real dent in the world's carbon emissions and a far better experience for homeowners.

We're now looking for a Design Engineer who wants to design & ship exceptional outcomes for users. Most of our product is a front end over hard physics (heat-loss calculations, hydronic design, LiDAR floor plans, compliance that has to be right), used by installers on a phone, with no signal, in a hurry. Making that feel simple is a design problem and an engineering problem at the same time, and this role sits right on that seam.

 

🌲 About Spruce

  • Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.

  • We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.

  • We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have grown the team 3x and revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, are launching an end-to-end solar and battery product in November, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed…

 

🥖 The role

You'll own how the product looks, feels and behaves wherever installers use it, from the first sketch to the shipped feature. Installers only adopt Spruce if it's easy to use on a real job, and adoption is what drives our growth. That puts your work at the centre of the business. Day-to-day you'll be:

  • Designing and shipping – You'll take a flow from rough idea all the way to production, prototyping in whatever gets you to an answer fastest (often code, sometimes Figma or a sketch), and testing with installers as you go. The gap between "we should fix this" and "it's fixed" is often a day.

  • Owning the interaction layer – You'll build and look after the component library and the patterns underneath it: motion, loading and empty states, touch targets that still work with gloves on. The small things that make a complex tool feel simple.

  • Building the parts that are hard to get right – The canvas-based floor plan and system design tools, the offline survey app (incl. LiDAR), the proposals homeowners see. These are the parts where the UI is the product, and where we've got the most still to build.

  • Raising the bar on everything we ship – You'll work closely with our product designers and developers, pairing on their work and reviewing it, so the quality of what you build rubs off on the rest of the product.

  • Spending time with installers – You'll go out on site, watch how the product actually gets used, then come back and change it.

You'll report to Steph, our co-founder and CPO (she’s pretty awesome) and you’ll work alongside Dan & Arron who’ve cooked up some incredible work in their time so far.

 

🫵 About you

We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft. You might currently call yourself a designer who ships, a front-end engineer with strong design instincts, or already a design engineer. We're looking for 3+ years of experience (and potentially a lot more) designing and building product UI, ideally in a startup or a fast-paced, impact-focussed team. We'd love to speak with you if you have:

  • Real taste, and shipped work to prove it – You can show us production UI you designed and built, and talk about why the details are the way they are. Work you'd happily put next to the best-crafted B2B products out there.

  • Strong design craft, and a real appetite for code – You're a strong designer first. You don't need to be a front-end engineer, and you might well ship with Cursor or Claude Code, but you want to understand the code you're shipping. Bonus for React and TypeScript depth, canvas/WebGL, animation, or complex state on mobile.

  • A prototyping instinct – You'd rather build a rough version and test it than argue about it in a doc. You're comfortable with things being imperfect in front of users.

  • Systems thinking – You enjoy the structure of a good component library and understand that consistency is what lets a small team ship fast. You also know when to slow down first: you value time spent on lo-fi wireframes and on understanding the data model before anything gets polished.

  • Curiosity about the domain – You want to understand how heating systems, solar and battery actually work, and you pick up technical detail fast. By the end of week two you'll be arguing about the best way to show a homeowner their solar self-consumption.

 

🌟 Our offer

  • 💰 £60-110k salary, depending on experience and location

  • 🍰 Meaningful slice of equity (options) in the company

  • 🏖️ 33 days holiday (25 plus bank holidays) and opportunity to work from abroad for another 30 days each year

  • 🏡 Hybrid working: 2–3 days in-person a week (London or Bristol), with full-team meetups every fortnight

  • 🏥 Private Medical Cover (Vitality)

  • 👧 Workplace Nursery Benefit scheme (YellowNest)

  • 🧑‍🍼 Enhanced Parental Leave

  • 🚲 Cycle to Work scheme

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Brilliant team to learn from and massive opportunity to grow

 

🧑‍💻 Working at Spruce

  • We're currently a close-knit team of 34, split between London and Bristol. We spend 2-3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone together every fortnight.

  • You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense.

  • We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then be able to rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions. This is clearly particularly important for this role but you'll be surrounded by a whole team who are also close to our customers.

  • We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. When things break, we focus on how we fix it, what we can learn, and never blame. You'll own your outcomes whilst knowing the team has your back.

  • Feedback is constant, direct, and kind. We'll tell you when something isn't working and expect the same honesty (and empathy) back.

Compensation: £60K – £110K • Offers Equity

title: Director of Customer Service & Complaints
descriptionHtml:
Ambition has no passport. That belief is why LemFi exists. We're the financial engine for people the world wasn't built to serve, the millions who move countries to build something better and find the financial system hasn't caught up with them yet. We started with remittances: the money people send home to the people they love. Now we run multi-currency accounts, Savings, eSIMs and Credit. Because staying connected to home and building somewhere new are not two separate things. They never were.

About the role

LemFi moves over $2B a month for 2M+ customers across 30+ countries. Behind every transfer is a customer service and complaints organisation that is growing fast and needs to get smarter, not just bigger. This Director role sits at the top of that organisation: 175 people across multiple locations, reporting directly to the COO, with a mandate to build a more efficient, scalable, and technology-enabled operation.


You will set the global vision, own the end-to-end complaints process under FCA and other regulatory frameworks, and make the calls that matter: where we concentrate operations, how much we do in-house versus BPO, and which automation and AI bets we place with Product and Tech. The right person will leave this role having fundamentally changed how a global fintech delivers support at scale.

What you'll build and own

  • Set the global strategy and operating model for a 175-person CS and complaints organisation, with a clear path to scale without proportional headcount growth

  • Own the end-to-end complaints process, ensuring full compliance with FCA requirements and other regulatory frameworks while keeping the experience fast and customer-centric

  • Define and execute the global location strategy: where we concentrate operations and why

  • Build and own the in-house vs BPO framework, including business case, vendor selection, and ongoing performance management if BPO partners are introduced

  • Partner with Product, Tech, and Design to identify and ship automation and AI initiatives that reduce manual contacts and improve cost-to-serve

  • Lead, develop, and hold to account a senior leadership bench across frontline support, escalations, and complaints

  • Define and execute the KPI framework (CSAT, resolution time, automation rate, cost-to-serve, complaints MI) and own the reporting to ExCo, Board, and regulators

Your experience

  • 10+ years of leadership in customer service, operations, or complaints inside a regulated business, fintech or banking preferred

  • Has run large, multi-location CS teams and demonstrably improved the global delivery model, not just maintained it

  • Has built or owned an in-house vs BPO strategy end to end, including location analysis, vendor evaluation, and contract management

  • Solid working knowledge of FCA complaints handling rules, including DISP, and experience owning complaints MI and regulatory reporting

  • Has personally driven efficiency improvements through tooling, automation, or AI, with measurable outcomes on cost-to-serve or contact volume

  • Track record of building strong second-line leadership, promoting from within and hiring well for senior manager roles

  • Comfortable with the data: owns the KPI framework, reads the numbers, and uses them to make decisions and to challenge the team

Nice to have

  • Exposure to multi-corridor remittance or cross-border payments, where the customer and regulatory profile differs by market

  • Experience embedding AI-assisted triage, deflection, or resolution tooling at meaningful scale

  • Board or ExCo-level reporting experience, including presenting to a regulator


Why join LemFi?

Your work here puts money back into families' pockets. That's the reward, and the weight of it. You'll take on some of the hardest problems in finance alongside people who do their best work when the stakes are real. We move fast and we expect a lot, because our customers can't afford for us to do otherwise. In return you get room to own real problems, global impact you can see, and a team that won't slow you down.

Bring grit and ownership and there's a place for them here. Ambition belongs here, come and show us yours.

Follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram and if you haven't already, download the app on the App Store or Google Play.


Don't feel that you're right for this role, but want to submit your interest in working for LemFi? You can join our talent community to stay in touch for future opportunities.

Recruitment agencies notice

LemFi does not accept unsolicited CVs from recruitment agencies. We work only with agencies on our preferred supplier list, and only when we’ve asked them for their support. Any CVs sent to us outside this arrangement will not incur a fee.

AI in hiring at LemFi

We use AI to cut admin, like notetakers that let interviewers focus on the conversation instead of typing. AI never makes hiring decisions. That responsibility always sits with our hiring teams. Read our AI use policy to see how we use AI and how we expect you to use it too.

title: Director of Engineering, KYX
descriptionHtml:
ABOUT TIDE

At Tide, we help SMEs save time and money in the running of their businesses by not only offering business accounts and related banking services, but also a comprehensive set of highly usable and connected administrative solutions, from invoicing to accounting.

Tide is transforming the small business banking market and now supports over 2 million members globally across the UK, Germany and France.

Using advanced technology, all solutions are designed with SMEs in mind. With quick onboarding, low fees and innovative features, we thrive on making data driven decisions to serve our mission: to help SMEs save time and money so they can get back to doing what they love.

Tide facts:

  • Tide is available for UK, German and French SMEs
  • Over 2 million members globally and rapidly growing
  • Over $300 million raised in funding
  • 3,000 Tideans globally
  • We have offices in Central London, with a member support and technology centre in Sofia, Bulgaria, technology centres in Serbia, Romania, Lithuania and Hyderabad and offices in Gurugram, New Delhi, Berlin, Paris and Luxembourg

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Tide is hiring a Director of Engineering to lead the engineering organisation behind KYX (KYC and KYB). Our vision for KYX is a world where every genuine business, business owner, their team, and everyone connected to them, onboards to Tide in minutes, unlocks the products they need as they grow, and never has to think twice about their data, while we identify bad actors, stop them at the door, continuously review their activity and off-board them the moment they're found.

You will be accountable for engineering strategy, organisation and execution across three domains. Onboarding KYX covers identity and access for registration and login, due diligence policy execution and vendor orchestration across the onboarding journey, and the risk scoring and agentic AI that assesses new applicants. Continuous KYX covers ongoing due diligence through periodic and event-triggered reviews, and how business owners bring their own team members onto their account. Risk Scoring is the KYX Scoring & ML team whose models power decisions across both domains.

This role sits at the intersection of regulated risk operations, member-facing conversion and applied AI. KYX Ops and KYX Policy set the rules you build for, Second Line of Defence sets the risk appetite, and our regulators set the bar. We need someone who can raise onboarding conversion and due diligence quality while driving the cost of KYX servicing per member down, and who can scale agentic solutions into workflows where a wrong answer has consequences for a member and for Tide.

As Director of Engineering, KYX you will

  • Own the engineering strategy and organisation for KYX, from onboarding identity, access and due diligence through continuous monitoring to risk scoring, unifying leadership that today sits in separate Onboarding and Continuous KYX lines.
  • Lead engineering across backend, frontend, data science and ML engineering, distributed across Hyderabad, Delhi, Sofia, Belgrade, Bucharest and Vilnius.
  • Own KYX Scoring & ML as a shared capability serving both onboarding and ongoing decisioning, including the model lifecycle end to end from development through backtesting and staged rollout to production monitoring.
  • Scale agentic AI in regulated workflows, from onboarding risk scoring through to screening, review and verification, in line with Tide's agentic governance framework.
  • Work with KYX Ops, KYX Policy, Second Line of Defence and Product across the UK, EU and India, and with IAM on the still-to-be-sharpened boundary around login and access.
  • Deliver measurable outcomes: higher automated decisioning rates, better due diligence and screening quality, and a falling KYX cost per member.
  • Build once, deploy globally, and keep market-specific logic isolated.

This is one of the most important engineering roles at Tide. You will shape how quickly and how well we onboard members, how confidently we scale into new markets under our own licences, and how far applied AI can compound into a lasting advantage in a regulated environment.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR:

  • Experience leading engineering organisations in identity, onboarding, fraud, financial crime or another regulated decisioning domain.
  • Strong track record of turning platform investment into measurable outcomes: conversion, due diligence quality, unit economics and workflow automation.
  • Experience taking machine learning from development into production at scale, and owning model performance once live.
  • Experience operating in a regulated environment, working with Ops, Policy and second line risk and compliance functions,
  • Strong judgement across organisation design, delivery, platform strategy, data architecture and technical quality.
  • Ability to lead distributed teams across multiple markets and unify previously separate engineering lines behind one roadmap.
  • Experience deploying AI or agentic systems inside regulated workflows, with a clear view on governance, evaluation and human oversight, would be a bonus.

WHAT YOU’LL GET IN RETURN:

Our location-specific employee benefits are designed to cater to the unique needs of Tideans:

  • Competitive Compensation –  Competitive salary and share options.
  • Time Off – Generous annual leave on top of bank holidays.
  • Parental Leave – Paid maternity, paternity, and adoption leave to support your family journey.
  • Sabbatical – Extended unpaid and paid leave options after completing milestone years with Tide.
  • Access to salary sacrifice benefits – like Nursery (could save up to 47% on fees!) and Cycle to Work discounts
  • Health Insurance – Comprehensive Private family insurance plan.
  • Life & Accident Cover – Comprehensive accidental and life insurance protection.
  • Mental Wellbeing – Access to therapy sessions, courses, meditations, and workshops.
  • Retirement Planning – Build your retirement fund faster with Tide’s pension scheme on eligible earnings.
  • Volunteering & Development Days – Paid days annually for volunteering or personal growth.
  • Learning & Development – Annual budget for books, courses, coaching, and more.
  • WOO (Work Outside the Office) – Work from abroad for up to 90 days annually.
  • Home Office Setup – Contribution towards setting up your home office
  • Laptop Ownership – Keep your old laptop and get a new one when it’s time for a replacement.
  • Snacks & Meals – Daily breakfast spread with all-day coffee, tea, and juices.

TIDEAN WAYS OF WORKING

At Tide, we champion a flexible workplace model thatsupports both in-person and remote work to cater to the specific needs of our different teams. 

While remote work is supported, we believe in the power of face-to-face interactions to foster team spirit and collaboration. Our offices are designed as hubs for innovation and team-building, where we encourage regular in-person gatherings to foster a strong sense of community.

#LI-AC1 #LI-Remote

TIDE IS A PLACE FOR EVERYONE

At Tide, we believe that we can only succeed if we let our differences enrich our culture. Our Tideans come from a variety of backgrounds and experience levels. We consider everyone irrespective of their ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran, neurodiversity or differently-abled status. We celebrate diversity in our workforce as a cornerstone of our success. Our commitment to a broad spectrum of ideas and backgrounds is what enables us to build products that resonate with our members’ diverse needs and lives. 

We are One Team and foster a transparent and inclusive environment, where everyone’s voice is heard.

title: Director of Legal, Compliance and Co-Sec
descriptionHtml:
Born in 1971, the roots of Mulberry are in Somerset, England. For more than fifty years, Mulberry has been a British lifestyle brand, internationally acclaimed for quality and design capturing the Mulberry Spirit.
Sustainability has been part of the Mulberry ethos since the brand's inception, in recognition of our purpose-driven approach, in 2024 we proudly achieved B Corp Certification.
Today, we are a global brand, but our values remain the same; we are committed to improving our impact on people and the planet. To do this our people are honest, dynamic, and community spirited.
If these are values you share, we would love you to join our team.

Scope of the Role:

Reporting to the CFO, the Director of Legal, Compliance and Co-Sec will be responsible for leading our global legal and corporate governance matters. This is a complex and critical role upholding exemplary legal advice and processes across our global operations. A key requirement will be ensuring the legal function is business enabling, building robust stakeholder relationships and acting as a trusted advisor. The Company Secretary element of the role is supported by an Assistant Co Sec and vital for compliant and clear operation of the Board.

They will also be responsible for all aspects of Health & Safety with a dedicated Health & Safety Manager.

A deep understanding of business risks in the macro climate as well as specific legal and contract risks will be necessary, as the department looks to develop an enterprise risk approach.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Legal:

  • Serve as the principal legal advisor to the business on all legal matters.
  • Draft, review, and negotiate a wide range of commercial agreements, including supplier, distribution, franchising, IP, marketing, e-commerce & SAAS contracts.
  • Advise on international regulatory frameworks including consumer protection, employment, and trade compliance.
  • Lead the resolution of performance or other contractual issues arising from ongoing supplier arrangements including resolving contentious matters
  • Oversee dispute resolution, litigation, and manage external counsel relationships globally.
  • Maintain a database of contracts and summary of terms, and look to develop a central hub of contracts, lease agreements and other key documentation for the business
  • Undertake research, horizon scanning and identification of issues which may impact the business, ensuring projects align with regulatory requirements
  • Identify key legal risks, advising on their implications for the Group and supporting the business by providing clear, pragmatic, solution-focused advice
  • Lead the development of an Enterprise Risk Framework for the business.

Compliance:

  • Develop, implement, and oversee the global compliance framework, ensuring adherence to legal, regulatory, and ethical standards.
  • Manage policies and training on anti-bribery & corruption, anti-money laundering, data protection (GDPR), ESG regulations, and whistleblowing.
  • Monitor changes in laws and regulations across jurisdictions to assess impact and ensure proactive compliance.

Co-Sec / Governance:

  • Oversee the Company Secretary for the Board and its Committees, ensuring compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure the organisation of Board and Committee meetings and preparation of agendas, minutes, resolutions, and maintain corporate records.
  • Ensure timely filings and regulatory submissions across global jurisdictions.
  • Oversee and support to advise Board members on governance matters, directors' duties, and corporate structure.
  • Oversee the management of subsidiary governance and legal entity management globally.

Culture:

  • Embrace and demonstrate the Mulberry values and behaviours: honesty, dynamism, and a community-oriented spirit.
  • Support Mulberry to deliver an inclusive culture, through behaving in a way that is open-minded and respectful towards others, and understanding that your views, opinions, and experiences may not always be shared by your colleagues.
  • Act as an ambassador for Mulberry and communicate positively about the brand.

Sustainability:

  • As a certified B Corp, we are committed to using business as a force for good. You’ll be encouraged to incorporate environmentally and socially responsible practices into your work, supporting our Made to Last strategy across Climate, Circularity, and Community.
  • Help foster a culture where diversity is celebrated and every individual feels valued, respected, and included. Champion equity, empathy, and understanding in all interactions - internally and externally.

Skills and Experience Required:

  • UK Qualified Solicitor with significant in-house legal experience at Director of Legal, Legal Director or General Counsel level.
  • Experience working in a UK listed business, with multiple entities.
  • Corporate governance expertise.
  • Excellent track record of managing legal risk and compliance.
  • Strong influencing and stakeholder management skills, prior experience with Board level exposure.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to build robust stakeholder and peer relationships to foster collaboration and team spirit.
  • Excellent team leadership skills.
  • Flexibility to work 3-4 days per week on-site in London with regular travel to our Somerset site.

title: Electrical Engineer (Electronic Warfare)
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

As a Hardware (Electronics) Engineer within our Electronic Warfare team, you will design and develop the RF hardware and electronic front-ends at the core of our electronic warfare and signal intelligence systems – from concept to field deployment. You will work hand-in-hand with system, software and mechanical teams to turn architecture needs into robust, high-performance hardware, and to ensure overall performance, robustness and reliability.

Responsibilities

  • RF Front-End Design: Design and develop radio and radar RF front-ends, from specification through to validation.

  • Hardware Architecture: Drive the hardware architecture of EW/SIGINT systems, ensuring performance, robustness and manufacturability.

  • High-Power & High-Voltage Electronics: Design high-power switching supplies (including narrow pulse generation) and high-voltage PCBs, supplies and shielding.

  • Integration & Validation: Lead board bring-up, RF integration, prototyping and validation against performance targets.

  • Technical Coordination: Collaborate across software, mechanical, GNC and ML teams on system integration and technical interfaces.

  • System Reviews & Documentation: Contribute to design and architecture reviews, maintaining consistency between requirements, design and testing.

Candidate Requirements

  • Strong background in RF hardware design is mandatory, including radio or radar front-end design.

  • No prior Electronic Warfare experience required.

  • Experience in RF integration is a plus.

  • Experience with high-power switching supplies (narrow pulse generation) is a definite plus.

  • Experience with high-voltage PCB / supply design and shielding.

  • MSc in Electrical / Electronics Engineering; PhD is a plus.

  • Broad engineering culture with understanding of mechanical, software and embedded systems.

  • Rigorous, structured and mission-driven mindset with strong analytical skills.

  • Excellent communication and documentation abilities.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

Foundational is building the most precise picture of Earth and orbit, using lasers fired from the ground. We call it ground truth for orbit.

title: Finance Manager
descriptionHtml:
Clôtures, facturation à l’usage, automatisation : la fonction finance d’Arkane Cloud est à construire, et c’est vous qui la structurez. Nous créons le poste de Finance Manager pour fiabiliser et automatiser la comptabilité, la facturation et le reporting, aux côtés de notre CFO.

Qui sommes-nous ?

Arkane Cloud est un Cloud Service Provider lyonnais, conçu pour l’IA et hébergé en Europe, avec des datacenters à Paris et à Lyon.

Notre propre infrastructure GPU permet à des startups, des chercheurs et des entreprises de déployer leurs modèles en quelques minutes, dans le respect du RGPD et jusqu’à 70 % moins cher qu’avec un hyperscaler.

Notre ambition : bâtir un acteur européen de référence de l’infrastructure IA.

Pourquoi ce poste ?

Arkane Cloud passe de 10 à 50 personnes d’ici fin 2027 et prépare des étapes structurantes : organisation de ses activités et financement de son infrastructure GPU. Pour réussir, il faut des comptes fiables chaque mois, une facturation automatisée et un reporting lisible par des investisseurs.

Rattaché(e) au CFO, vous êtes son point d’appui au quotidien, sur nos deux activités.

Vos missions

• Piloter la clôture mensuelle, pour des comptes livrés en J+10.

• Fiabiliser le chiffre d’affaires Cloud : facturation à l’heure, capacité GPU réservée, prépaiements.

• Structurer puis automatiser les processus finance, avec un objectif clair : 90 % des flux automatisés, 10 % de validation manuelle.

• Consolider le reporting du groupe, avec une vision claire du Cloud et du Négoce.

• Éclairer les décisions stratégiques du CFO et accompagner les projets structurants : financements, data rooms, futur audit.

Vos 6 premiers mois

• 1er mois : prise en main des outils et des flux, plan d’action partagé avec le CFO.

• 3 mois : calendrier de clôture en place, règles de chiffre d’affaires Cloud documentées, comptes mensuels livrés en J+10.

• 6 mois : facturation et rapprochements bancaires largement automatisés, reporting mensuel consolidé livré chaque mois.

Votre expérience

• Environ 5 ans en finance, idéalement entre cabinet d’audit et entreprise.

• Une expérience en scale-up tech, SaaS ou cloud.

• Une formation DSCG, master CCA, école de commerce ou équivalent.

Vos expertises

• Clôture et comptabilité générale : saisie et récupération de la comptabilité, clôtures mensuelles et annuelles, pilotage d’un cabinet.

• Chiffre d’affaires : abonnements, facturation à l’usage, prépaiements.

• Outils : Pennylane ou équivalent, Excel avancé, Stripe, GoCardless et CRM (HubSpot).

• Contrôle de gestion : budget, reporting mensuel, indicateurs de pilotage.

• Gestion de projet : mise en place d’outils et documentation des processus.

Un vrai plus :
