title: Montu Pharmacy Assessment Centre
descriptionHtml:
Ready to start or take the next step in your pharmacy career?

At Montu, we are doing things differently, and that includes how we recruit.

We are growing, and we are looking for enthusiastic, hardworking and patient-focused individuals to join our pharmacy team in Winnersh Triangle.

Whether you are looking to take your first step into healthcare, explore a new career in pharmacy or bring your existing pharmacy experience to a rapidly growing organisation, we would love to meet you.

We are hosting a Pharmacy Assessment Centre on Saturday 5th December, giving you the opportunity to experience a different approach to recruitment, demonstrate your skills and learn more about what it is like to work at Montu.

You do not need previous pharmacy experience for all of our opportunities. For our entry-level positions, what matters most is your attitude, willingness to learn and genuine commitment to making a difference to patients.

Our pharmacy is busy. Really busy. It is a lively, energetic environment where things move quickly, teamwork is essential and no two days are quite the same. If you enjoy being on your feet, working alongside others and being part of a team where everyone has a role to play, you could feel right at home.

Behind every prescription we process is a patient relying on us to get things right. Whether you are packing medication, dispensing prescriptions or completing final accuracy checks, your contribution matters.

Opportunities Available

We are recruiting across several positions within our pharmacy team, with opportunities for both experienced pharmacy professionals and individuals looking to enter the industry.

Pharmacy Assistant

An excellent entry point into the pharmacy sector, with no previous pharmacy experience required.

You will support the day-to-day operations of our busy pharmacy, including preparing orders, packing medication, supporting stock management and helping ensure prescriptions are processed accurately and efficiently.

We are looking for individuals who are organised, reliable, comfortable with repetitive tasks and enjoy working in a hands-on, fast-paced environment.

Trainee Pharmacy Dispenser

Looking to develop a career in pharmacy? This could be your opportunity.

No previous dispensing experience is required. You will receive training and support as you develop the knowledge and practical skills needed to work within our dispensing team.

You will learn about prescription processing, medication handling, accuracy, pharmacy procedures and the importance of maintaining high standards of patient safety.

Pharmacy Dispenser

For individuals with an existing dispensing qualification and experience working within a pharmacy environment.

You will support the safe and accurate dispensing of prescriptions, working closely with pharmacists, technicians and the wider pharmacy team.

You will need excellent attention to detail, a strong understanding of pharmacy procedures and the ability to maintain accuracy while managing high prescription volumes.

Accuracy Checking Dispenser

We are looking for qualified and experienced Accuracy Checking Dispensers who can help maintain the high standards of accuracy and patient safety expected within our pharmacy.

You will undertake accuracy checking duties within the scope of your qualification, training and authorisation, supporting the efficient processing of prescriptions and working collaboratively with the wider team.

Accuracy Checking Technician (ACT)

For qualified Pharmacy Technicians with an accredited accuracy checking qualification and current GPhC registration.

You will play an important role in maintaining dispensing accuracy, supporting pharmacy operations and ensuring our processes meet the required professional and regulatory standards.

You will bring confidence, attention to detail and the ability to work effectively in a high-volume dispensing environment.

What Is Our Pharmacy Assessment Centre?

We know that traditional interviews do not always give people the best opportunity to demonstrate what they can do.

That is why we are taking a slightly different approach.

Our Pharmacy Assessment Centre is designed to be an engaging, practical and interactive experience where you can demonstrate your abilities, meet members of the Montu team and gain a better understanding of our working environment.

You can expect a combination of practical and team-based activities designed to assess skills relevant to working within our pharmacy, including:

  • Attention to detail and accuracy

  • Literacy and the ability to follow written instructions

  • Working effectively with others

  • Organisation and the ability to follow processes

  • Speed and efficiency without compromising accuracy

  • Communication and problem-solving

We are not expecting everyone to arrive with pharmacy knowledge, particularly those applying for our entry-level opportunities.

We are interested in how you approach tasks, how you work with others and whether you have the right attitude to succeed in our environment.

What happens after the assessment centre?

Candidates who successfully complete the assessment centre will be invited to attend a further on-site interview at Montu on a later date.

Please note that attendance at the assessment centre does not guarantee an interview or offer of employment.

What Are We Looking For?

We are looking for people who genuinely want to be part of a team making a difference.

Our ideal candidates will be:

  • Patient-focused: You understand that the work you do has a direct impact on the people relying on our service.

  • Detail-oriented: Accuracy matters, particularly when working with medication.

  • Comfortable in a busy environment: You enjoy an energetic workplace and can remain focused when things get hectic.

  • Reliable and hardworking: You take pride in doing your job well and supporting the people around you.

  • Team players: You understand that pharmacy operations depend on people working together.

  • Adaptable: You are comfortable learning new processes and responding to change.

  • Eager to learn: Whether you are new to pharmacy or already experienced, you are motivated to develop your skills.

You do not need to be the loudest person in the room or have years of experience to succeed here.

What matters is your work ethic, your attention to detail and your commitment to doing things properly.

About Montu

Montu is a leading medical cannabis company working to improve access to cannabis-based medicines for patients across the UK.

Through our specialist clinical services and pharmacy operations, we support patients receiving prescribed cannabis-based medicines for a range of eligible medical conditions.

Our multidisciplinary teams bring together clinicians, pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, dispensers and operational colleagues, all working towards the same goal: delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care.

We are a rapidly growing organisation, and our pharmacy is at the heart of what we do.

Every prescription represents a patient who is depending on us. From the moment a prescription reaches our pharmacy to the moment medication is dispatched, every member of our team plays an important role in that patient journey.

We are proud to be helping shape an evolving area of healthcare, and we want people who are excited to be part of that journey.

Why Join Montu?

Joining Montu means becoming part of a growing organisation where your work has purpose and your contribution makes a difference.

We offer:

  • Competitive salaries dependent on the position, qualifications and experience

  • Opportunities for training and professional development

  • Career progression within our growing pharmacy operations

  • A supportive and collaborative team environment

  • The opportunity to gain experience within a specialist area of healthcare

  • The chance to be part of a growing business helping improve patient access to prescribed medication

Further information about the benefits applicable to each role will be provided during the recruitment process.

Ready to Join Us?

Assessment Centre: Saturday 5th December

Location: Winnersh Triangle, Berkshire

If you are looking for an opportunity to begin a career in pharmacy, develop your existing skills or take the next step within a growing healthcare organisation, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now to be considered for a place at our Pharmacy Assessment Centre.

Following an initial review of applications, shortlisted candidates will receive further information about the assessment centre, including timings, location details and what to expect on the day.

title: MSF International Managing Director
descriptionHtml:
Location: Based in Geneva or within approximately +/- two (2) hours from Geneva

Contract: Fixed term at 100% - It is a mandated role (currently 3+3 years)

Starting date: 01st of March 2027

Deadline to apply: 26th of November 2026 - We reserve the right to close this position once suitable candidates have been identified.

Compensation and Benefits: MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract

*By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that.

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

MSF International

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

I. CONTEXT

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent medical humanitarian organisation providing emergency assistance to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters, based solely on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.

MSF International is the legal entity whose membership is composed of all MSF associations. It hosts the International Secretariat, supports the International Board, facilitates coordination across the MSF movement, and provides shared services and initiatives as mandated by the movement.

Within MSF International, the International Office acts as the Secretariat of the International Board (IB) and operates under the direct management of the International Secretary General (ISG). MSF International also provides administrative and operational support to movement-wide initiatives and services, including MSF Access.

II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The MSF International Managing Director is a senior executive role responsible for institutional leadership, stewardship of resources, and organizational performance of MSF International as a legal entity serving the MSF movement.

The role ensures that MSF International:

  • Effectively implements -within the scope of MSF International - the MSF International Multiyear Plan and SPARC (MSF-wide Strategic Planning, Accountability and Resource Cycle) and supports the International Board and the International Secretary General in their governance roles and responsibilities.

  • Provides high quality, well governed services to the MSF movement, as mandated by the Full ExCom (executive committee);

  • Operates with strong systems of governance, accountability, risk management and duty of care;

  • Has robust, transparent and efficient governance, financial, human, and knowledge systems;

  • Operates as a coherent, inclusive, and accountable internationally distributed organization;

  • Models MSF values in leadership, equity, duty of care, and ethical management;

  • Ensures that the decisions taken by the Board of Directors of MSF International and its implementation is compliant with the Articles of Association, the internal regulations, as well as Swiss standards and Swiss laws, for as long as the registered office is in Geneva, Switzerland.

The MSF Management Director acts as a strategic partner to the International Secretary General, providing leadership on transversal and institutional topics with regards to the management of MSF International.

III. ACCOUNTABILITIES

1. Strategic Leadership and Implementation of MSF International (Multi‑year Plan & SPARC): Lead the translation of MSF International and movement strategic priorities into clear objectives, organisational plans, policies and resourcing within MSF International; support cross‑functional initiatives required by international platforms as needed to deliver the Multi‑Year Strategic Plan and SPARC commitments.

Expected result: MSF International delivers on agreed strategic priorities and SPARC commitments through coherent plans, measurable milestones and coordinated delivery across functions and movement partners.

a. Contribute to the development of MSF International Multi‑year Strategic Plan and SPARC within MSF International’s mandate and scope and translate strategic priorities into concrete organisational objectives, policies, systems and resource allocations, ensuring coherence across functions and services.

b. Supports cross‑functional and transversal initiatives required to deliver common strategic priorities and SPARC‑related commitments.

c. Contribute to movement-wide discussions on harmonization, efficiency and shared services.

d. Sets up and tracks implementation plans, including key milestones, indicators, and risks. Support the ISG in reporting to the International Board and relevant Standing Committees, and contribute to SPARC’s Monitoring & Evaluation Framework and Expense Steering Process for functions and services managed within MSF International’s scope.

e. Deputize for the ISG as required, within agreed scope and representation mandates.

f. Represent MSF International to key stakeholders, partners and external audiences as required, and build relationships that protect and advance MSF's institutional interests.

2. Governance, legal compliance, accountability and risk management for MSF-International: Ensure robust governance implementation, statutory compliance and effective risk management systems for MSF International as a Swiss legal entity and for services delivered on behalf of the movement; prepare governance-level advice and support Board decision-making.

Expected result: International Board and executive decisions are supported by timely, compliant and risk‑informed advice; MSF International statutory obligations and legal requirements are met and organisational risks are identified and mitigated.

a. Act as senior management liaison to the ISG, the International Board and Standing Committees on matters related to MSF International organisational governance, resources, risk, compliance and organisational performance.

b. Ensure robust systems of internal control, risk management and accountability, are in place and functioning for MSF International, in line with legal, fiduciary and associative obligations, including preparedness for critical incidents directly affecting MSF International.

c. Lead or support organizational responses to critical incidents directly affecting MSF International, including HR, legal, reputational, safeguarding or security‑related situations.

d. Ensure that MSF International fulfils its statutory responsibilities as a Swiss legal entity and that appropriate legal, administrative and governance support is obtained for decisions of the IB in light of the International Statutes, the Internal Regulations, and Swiss standards and law. Ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations regarding daily management of MSF International.

e. Oversee compliance with GDPR and Swiss data protection law, promoting a culture of privacy and responsible data use.

f. Ensure appropriate legal review of all contracts and agreements directly involving MSF International and including those through which it delivers services to the movement, in accordance with MSF’s rules and policies, as well as Swiss law.

g. Design, implement and monitor the effectiveness of internal control systems and procedures; ensure that MSF International risks are identified and registered and ensure that mitigation measures are discussed and incorporated in the respective departments annual plans.

3. Services to MSF: Provide executive stewardship of movement-wide services mandated to MSF International, ensuring clear service governance, defined accountabilities and cost‑effective delivery.

Expected result: Movement services operate to agreed service charters and KPIs, with transparent costs and reliable delivery that meet sections' needs and contractual obligations.

a. Provide executive leadership and stewardship over services mandated to MSF International in support of the MSF movement, ensuring they are clearly governed, fit for purpose, cost‑effective and appropriately funded.

b. Ensure that roles, responsibilities, decision‑making authority and service boundaries between MSF International and MSF sections are clearly defined and communicated, balancing interoperability and mutualization objectives with the sections and ODs autonomy.

c. Establish and monitor service governance and performance frameworks, including service charters, KPIs, cost‑sharing arrangements and escalation mechanisms where relevant, and ensure transparency.

d. Facilitate structured dialogue with MSF sections to identify service needs, manage expectations and address risks or performance issues.

4. Financial stewardship and institutional integrity: Oversee budgeting, financial planning, statutory accounts, audits and financial controls; ensure alignment of resources with strategic priorities and manage institutional financial and insurance arrangements.

Expected result: MSF International maintains sound financial health, regulatory compliance and transparent resource allocation that supports strategic objectives.

a. Provide executive oversight of budgeting, forecasting and financial reporting for MSF International.

b. Ensure alignment between strategic priorities (including SPARC) and resource allocation.

c. Oversee statutory accounts, audits, financial policies and compliance with Swiss GAAP, tax and VAT requirements.

d. Oversee relationships with external auditors, financial advisors and legal counsel.

e. Oversee institutional insurance coverage and financial risk mitigation. Manage the full suite of institutional and corporate insurance coverage for MSF International.

f. Oversee legacies and donations earmarked for MSF International

5. People, culture and organisational development: Oversee people strategy, workforce planning, performance management, leadership development and organisational design to foster an inclusive, safe and high‑performing culture across a distributed workforce.

Expected result: A diverse, supported and capable organisation with clear succession pathways, strong performance management and a positive organisational culture.

a. Provide strategic leadership over human resources management, organizational design and workforce planning.

b. Ensure a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct.

c. Oversee performance management, leadership development and succession planning.

d. Ensure a lively MSF International culture despite the geographical spread, including through adequate internal communication.

e. Lead organisational development, when necessary, to ensure the organisational structure remains fit for purpose and appropriate for a well-functioning office.

f. Manage institutional relationships with MSF sections hosting MSF International staff and ensure coherent frameworks for hosting, contracting, payroll and staff integration.

g. Ensure appropriate information governance and that knowledge management systems support collaboration, institutional memory and organizational learning, including learning from strategy and SPARC implementation.

h. Liaise regularly with the Staff Committee of MSF International.

IV. AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY

The MSF International Managing Director operates with a high degree of autonomy to think, interpret and act within the strategic direction set by the International Secretary General, the International Board and the governance framework of MSF International.

The role is required to make independent judgements on organisational priorities, resource allocation, risk mitigation, service performance, people matters and operational responses, often in situations where issues are sensitive, cross-functional and without straightforward precedent.

The complexity of the environment is significant: the postholder works across a federated MSF movement with multiple stakeholders, distributed teams, hosted staff arrangements and diverse section interests, while also ensuring compliance with Swiss legal and regulatory requirements, internal governance rules, financial and HR procedures, safeguarding standards and data protection obligations. Success therefore depends on balancing institutional coherence, legal and procedural rigour, and service effectiveness with diplomacy, sound judgement and the ability to operate in ambiguity.

V. SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.

  • Ensure respectful management and communication at all levels.

  • Ensure that staff and consultants under their supervision understand their responsibilities with respect to required behaviour and report abuse while working for MSF by reinforcing and regularly discussing expected standards of behaviour.

  • Welcome complainants, understand how to guide colleagues to appropriate channels, promote and create an environment that does not tolerate abuse or inappropriate behaviour. Guide colleagues to the correct process without investigating.

  • Ensure that staff know how to complain and keep staff updated on reporting mechanisms.


Education

  • Master’s degree in management, humanitarian affairs, political sciences, or a related field, or equivalent senior-level professional experience

Experience

  • Extensive senior leadership experience (General/Executive Director, Deputy Director or Director of a major organizational function) in a complex and large international and decentralised organisations

  • MSF experience is a major asset

  • Proven ability to operate at Board and executive level

  • Strong people leadership, including conflict management and change leadership

  • Solid expertise in financial oversight, governance and organisational systems

  • Experience with equity, diversity and inclusion strategies

Knowledge

  • Strong commitment to MSF’s humanitarian principles and associative values.

  • High level of integrity and ability to handle confidential and sensitive matters.

  • Knowledge of Swiss legal, institutional, employment, financial and data protection frameworks is an asset.

  • Familiarity with governance of associations and federated movements is an asset.

  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional and institutional change.

  • Comfortable leading teams across different locations and liaising with stakeholders at all levels.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, able to communicate complex or sensitive matters clearly, concisely, and professionally.

  • High level of discretion, judgement, and emotional intelligence, and the ability to build a strong network across an organisation.

  • Confident decision‑making and the ability to act autonomously as appropriate.

  • Flexible team player, willing to adapt to changes, and confident tackling unfamiliar challenges across multiple domains of knowledge/experience.

Languages

  • Excellent English (written and spoken) is essential.

  • French highly desirable, and other MSF languages are further assets.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding and acceptance of these recruitment procedures.

title: Oberbauleiter im Tiefbau (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung unseres Partners suchen wir einen Oberbauleiter im Tiefbau (m/w/d) im Großraum Hannover / Ostwestfalen-Lippe.

In dieser Position übernimmst Du eine Schlüsselrolle in einem stark wachsenden Unternehmen im Spezialtiefbau. Unser Partner denkt die klassische Baubranche neu und setzt auf digitale Transformation und partnerschaftliche Zusammenarbeit anstelle von starren Hierarchien.

Du verantwortest komplexe Infrastrukturprojekte, gestaltest die Projektstrategien aktiv mit und führst Dein Team auf Augenhöhe.

Aufgaben

  • Du durchdringst Großprojekte bereits vor dem ersten Spatenstich, analysierst Bodengutachten sowie Leistungsverzeichnisse (LVs) und leitest daraus die optimale Projekt- und Materialstrategie ab
  • Du steuerst eigenverantwortlich komplexe Bauvorhaben im Tiefbau und verantwortest die wirtschaftliche sowie technische Projektplanung
  • Du definierst klare Vorgaben für die Arbeitsvorbereitung, beurteilst digitale 3D-Modelle und treibst den Einsatz moderner Technologien wie Sensorik und Drohnenvermessung voran
  • Du übernimmst die fachliche und disziplinarische Führung von Bauleitern in einem wachsenden Team durch echtes Mentoring, forderst eigenverantwortliche Phasenpläne ein und entwickelst Dein Team kontinuierlich weiter
  • Du agierst als zentraler, strategischer Ansprechpartner für Kunden und Auftraggeber und repräsentierst das Unternehmen souverän, um langfristige Kundenbeziehungen zu sichern

Qualifikation

  • Du verfügst über mehrjährige Berufserfahrung in der eigenverantwortlichen Steuerung von komplexen Tiefbau-, Erdbau- oder Infrastrukturprojekten
  • Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium im Bauingenieurwesen oder eine gleichwertige Qualifikation und bringst fundiertes technisches Know-how mit
  • Du denkst unternehmerisch, triffst gerne eigenverantwortliche Entscheidungen und hast das Ziel, Bauabläufe datengestützt zu optimieren
  • Du bringst eine hohe Affinität für digitale Planungsmethoden mit und bist offen für innovative technologische Ansätze
  • Du überzeugst als wertschätzende Führungspersönlichkeit, die ihre Kollegen motiviert und fördert

Benefits

  • Du berichtest direkt an die Geschäftsführung und hast extrem viel Gestaltungsspielraum in einem stabil wachsenden Unternehmen
  • Dich erwartet ein attraktives Gehalt, welches durch einen stark leistungsorientierten Bonus signifikant ergänzt wird
  • Du arbeitest flexibel und ortsunabhängig: Ob im Homeoffice, vor Ort oder im Büro – Deine Arbeitsleistung wird durch Vertrauen und Ergebnisse bewertet, nicht durch starre Präsenzpflicht
  • Dir stehen 30 Tage Urlaub im Jahr sowie die Möglichkeit eines Dienstwagens, auch zur privaten Nutzung, zur Verfügung
  • Du bist Teil einer kollaborativen Lernkultur, in der Deine persönliche Entwicklung durch gezielte Schulungen und Weiterbildungsbudgets aktiv gefördert wird

Klingt spannend? Dann bewirb Dich jetzt! Deine Bewerbung wird selbstverständlich streng vertraulich behandelt. Durch die direkte Zusammenarbeit mit den Entscheidungsträgern garantieren wir Dir einen schnellen, transparenten und maßgeschneiderten Prozess.

Deine Ansprechpartnerin ist Marie-Janet Calzone. Du erreichst sie auch telefonisch unter der +49 1575 8283 261.

Wir freuen uns darauf, Dich kennenzulernen!

title: Office Manager
descriptionHtml:
Hou jij ervan om teams te ondersteunen en mensen te ontvangen met een glimlach? ACT agency, hét reclamebureau dat barst van de creativiteit, zoekt een enthousiaste Office Manager om ons team te versterken. Als jij klaar bent om jouw organisatorische vaardigheden naar een hoger niveau te tillen en een onmisbare schakel te worden binnen ons jonge en bruisende bureau, dan is deze vacature jou op het lijf geschreven!

Taken

Als Office Manager bij ACT agency krijg je de kans om een centrale rol te vervullen in onze dagelijkse kantooractiviteiten. Je werkt zij aan zij met ons energieke team van reclameprofessionals en zorgt ervoor dat alles op rolletjes loopt. Geen dag is hetzelfde! Je bent verantwoordelijk voor diverse administratieve taken en speelt een cruciale rol in het reilen en zeilen van ons kantoor. Van pandbeheer tot het verwelkomen van bezoekers en van het regelen van kantoorbenodigdheden tot het organiseren van inspirerende evenementen - jij bent de spin in het web.

Onze idealie kandidaat is een horecatijger die ervan houdt om andere mensen te helpen en te ontzorgen.

  • Beheer van de algemene e-mail- en telefoon, met een frisse en vriendelijke tone of voice die voor een glimlach bij onze klanten zorgt.
  • Ontvangen en begeleiden van bezoekers met een warm welkom en een dosis charme.
  • Coördineren van vergaderingen en deels processen, met ondersteuning van onze proces-manager, en het opstellen van documentatie die zowel professioneel als eigentijds is, zodat alle neuzen dezelfde kant op staan.
  • Ondersteuning bieden bij het beheren van kantoorbenodigdheden, waarbij je oog hebt voor details en creatieve oplossingen.
  • Het organiseren van leuke bedrijfsevenementen die onze klanten versteld doen staan en waar ze nog lang over napraten.
  • Ondersteunen bij diverse administratieve taken, zoals het pandbeheer en het eerste aanspreekpunt zijn voor onze onderhuurders en pandeigenaar.
  • Lunch bestellen en gereed maken voor collega's en klanten.

Vereisten

  • Deze vacature is voor 20 tot 24 uur per week. Er wordt verwacht dat je 3 dagen per week op kantoor aanwezig bent: op maandag, dinsdag en donderdag. Optioneel zijn de werktijden flexibel; denk aan van 8 tot 14 uur.
  • Je hebt relevante ervaring en het liefst ook horeca-ervaring.
  • Uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden in het Nederlands en Engels, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk, met een eigentijdse en pakkende schrijfstijl.
  • Je hebt een bruisende persoonlijkheid, bent proactief en toont initiatief.
  • Jouw energie en ideeën werken aanstekelijk!
  • Je bent georganiseerd, punctueel en hebt oog voor detail - jij zorgt ervoor dat niets aan onze aandacht ontsnapt.

Benefits

  • Een klantportfolio dat je elke dag uitdaagt om je talent te laten zien.
  • Een platte organisatie waarbij jouw mening telt.
  • Een gezellige en open werkomgeving.
  • Goede arbeidsvoorwaarden & ontwikkelingsmogelijkheden.
  • Een toffe werkplek in de Houthavens, een lekkere lunch, regelmatig borrels; straks bij lekker weer op ons grote dakterras.
  • Pensioen opbouw.
  • Onbeperkt vakantiedagen.
  • NS Businesskaart voor al je zakelijke reizen.
  • Optioneel deelname aan ons fietsplan.
  • MacBook + toebehoren om op kantoor en thuis goed te kunnen werken.

Klaar om de reclamewereld te veroveren met jouw talent en gezelligheid? Solliciteer nu en upload jouw CV en een overtuigende motivatiebrief. We kijken ernaar uit om jou te verwelkomen in ons team bij ACT agency!

title: Operational Service Intelligence Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Radiant

Radiant is building AI native cloud infrastructure for the most demanding compute workloads.

Our platform combines high density GPU compute, high performance networking, storage, data centre operations and cloud software. We design and operate infrastructure for customers who require predictable performance, strong security, operational resilience and clear service accountability.

As Radiant scales across multiple sites, regions and infrastructure environments, we are building the operational intelligence layer that connects technical performance with customer outcomes, commercial commitments and investment decisions.

About the role

The Operational Service Intelligence Manager will create the reporting, KPI and capacity-planning framework used across Radiant’s Service Management, Infrastructure Operations and Data Centre Operations teams.

You will turn operational data into clear insight for leadership, Finance, Customer Success, Product and Engineering. You will help the business understand service performance, customer impact, capacity constraints, infrastructure cost and opportunities for improvement.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can define the right metrics, build practical reporting and use data to improve how teams operate.

What you’ll do

  • Define and maintain KPIs for:

    • Incident, Change, Problem and Request Management

    • Infrastructure Operations and SRE

    • Data Centre Operations

    • Security-related operational activity

  • Establish customer-facing service reporting, including:

    • Availability and uptime

    • SLA performance

    • SLA credits and penalties

    • Incident and service trends

  • Build dashboards and reporting for operational performance, capacity and risk.

  • Own reporting standards, definitions and data quality across operational teams.

  • Analyse:

    • Compute, network and storage utilisation

    • Available and constrained capacity

    • Power usage and infrastructure efficiency

    • Failure rates and recurring incidents

    • Spare inventory and component usage

    • Vendor performance and RMA trends

  • Support capacity planning for GPU clusters, networks, storage and data centre infrastructure.

  • Develop SLA simulations and planning models, including hot and cold spare requirements.

  • Work with Finance on infrastructure reporting and FinOps, including:

    • Cost per MW

    • Cost per GPU hour

    • Asset inventory

    • Committed and available capacity

  • Partner with Customer Success to create consistent service reporting for customers.

  • Own the strategy for service intelligence and KPI tooling.

  • Identify operational bottlenecks and use data to recommend improvements.

  • Work with Product and Engineering to turn recurring service issues into product improvements.

  • Help define telemetry and observability requirements for new products and releases.

  • Measure how product changes affect operational KPIs and customer experience.

  • Lead quarterly service reviews with Product and Engineering leaders.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience in service intelligence, operational analytics, service management, infrastructure operations or a related field.

  • Strong experience defining KPIs, SLAs and operational reporting.

  • Experience working with ITSM, infrastructure, data centre or cloud operations teams.

  • Strong analytical and data visualisation skills.

  • Ability to work with operational data from multiple systems and identify meaningful trends.

  • Understanding of capacity planning, infrastructure utilisation and service performance.

  • Experience presenting concise, decision-ready reporting to senior stakeholders.

  • Commercial awareness and experience working with Finance or FinOps teams.

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work across technical and non-technical teams.

  • Comfortable building structure and reporting standards in a growing organisation.

Nice to have

  • Experience in AI infrastructure, HPC, cloud, hyperscale or data centre environments.

  • Experience with ITIL, service management or operational excellence frameworks.

  • Familiarity with GPU, network, storage and power-related infrastructure metrics.

  • Experience working with observability, telemetry or data platform teams.

  • Experience turning operational data into customer-facing product features.

Success in the role

  • Radiant has a consistent and trusted set of operational KPIs.

  • Leadership can quickly understand service health, capacity and risk.

  • Customer reporting is accurate, consistent and delivered on time.

  • Finance has reliable infrastructure cost and utilisation data.

  • Capacity constraints and vendor issues are identified early.

  • Operational trends consistently inform product and process improvements.

title: Operations Manager, Offer Operations
descriptionHtml:
At Joko, our mission is to we help consumers save time and money when shopping online or in-store.

Founded in Paris, Joko is a tech company and certified B Corp with over 120 talents across Paris, Barcelona, and New York (and beyond). More than 7 million users already save money every day at 10,000+ merchants with Joko.

From cashback and automatic coupons to price alerts, we've kept expanding our products to make shopping smarter. Today, Joko is an AI shopping app: with Juno, our shopping assistant, users can find the right product at the best price in only a few seconds, with recommendations that get sharper the more they use it.

Having reached profitability in our core market, we’re now scaling globally, with a strong focus on the US.

It’s still day 1, come build the future of shopping with us!

🦾 Our Offer Operations team

Joko helps millions of users earn cashback automatically, whether they shop online through affiliate links, activate coupons, or pay in-store with their linked bank card. Behind each of these experiences, there's an operational engine that needs to work flawlessly: transactions must be tracked, cashback must be caught, offers must be reliable, and merchants must perform as expected. When this engine breaks, users don't get paid — and trust erodes fast.

Offer Operations owns that engine. The team's mission is to guarantee the reliability and continuous improvement of Joko's core monetization mechanics — across affiliate tracking, coupons, card-linked bank integrations, gift cards, and merchant performance. It's a technical, data-heavy, high-stakes scope that sits right at the heart of what makes Joko's product work.

🎯 What you will do

As an Operations Manager, your main mission is to own one of the processes that decides whether millions of Joko users actually get the cashback they're owed. You'll report to David Le Pahun, our Offer Operations Lead. The role blends four things: analysing data, designing how the process should work, solving problems with AI, technologies or in the last resort outsourcing, and managing projects.

  • Analyse data. You'll build the dashboards that tell you — and everyone else — whether your part of the system is healthy: how many transactions are being correctly tracked and rewarded, what's silently breaking down, whether user experience is suffering.

  • Design the process. You decide how merchants get set up on our platform: their cashback rate, which purchases qualify, how we connect to their systems. A lot of this doesn't have a playbook yet — you'll be writing a good chunk of it as you go.

  • Solve problems with technology. A merchant might be showing users a coupon that doesn't actually pay out. A batch of card purchases might not match cleanly to any merchant we track. You'll dig into why, then fix it choosing the right solution for it: automating it with AI, improving one of our internal tools (built on Retool) and if a human is required, you'll build the right playbook to outsource it.

  • Manage outsourced resources. You'll manage the outsourced team members who help you operate at scale — briefing them, training them, checking their work is actually good — while juggling several of these issues at once and deciding what matters most.

  • Partner cross-functionally. With Product & Engineering when the fix is structural, and with the commercial team when it's really about a merchant relationship.

👀 Who we're looking for

  • Experience: around 2–5 years of experience, ideally with exposure to Operations, Product, or a technical/data-driven environment.

  • AI-native: you genuinely believe in what AI can do, and you already use it as part of how you work — not as a buzzword, but as a real way to automate the repetitive parts of your job and move faster on the rest.

  • Ops mindset: you think in systems — monitoring → detection → investigation → resolution → prevention. You instinctively look for what can break and build safeguards so it doesn't happen again.

  • Tech acumen: you're comfortable in a technical environment — tracking, APIs, integrations — and can hold your own in a conversation with Engineering.

  • Analytical skills: you're data-driven and comfortable navigating dashboards, investigating anomalies, and making decisions based on metrics.

  • Attention to detail: the devil is in the details, and you have a talent for spotting flaws where others don't.

  • Communication: clear written and verbal communication skills; you're not afraid to defend your decisions with demanding stakeholders (including merchants and the outsourced teams you'll be directing).

  • Education: Top-tier engineering or business school background. International experience and a double degree are a clear plus.

  • Languages: fluent in written and spoken English. Mastering French is not required.

💎 Our perks

(Some of the benefits listed below are available to full-time positions only)

At Joko, we believe that flexibility and trust are essential. Our work environment reflects this through:

  • Flexible remote : If you live in Paris, you can choose to work from our office or from home with no constraints. If you live elsewhere, we can provide access to a coworking space and a coworking budget.

  • Work from anywhere : Want to spend a month in Italy while working? You can work from most countries in the world for up to 3 months per year.

On top of that, we offer plenty of perks:

  • 💸 Top-market compensation

  • 📈 Equity for everyone with the chance to own a piece of what you build

  • 🤖 Half-day each week dedicated to leveling up with AI by exploring new tools, iterating hard, and sharpening your skills

  • 🌴 Yearly offsite in amazing locations and budget for team-building events & monthly in-person gatherings

  • 💪 Contribution to your ClassPass subscription

  • 🍼 8-week leave paid 100% for the second parent

  • …and much more, check the full list here!

🤝 Our hiring process

  1. Intro call: Quick screening with the Hiring Manager or the Talent team.

  2. Step 1 – Team interview (45 min): Conversation with two Joko team members (could include the Hiring Manager, people from the team you’d join, or colleagues from other teams).

  3. Step 2 – Role-specific assessments

    • For non-engineering roles: A take-home case study followed by a 45-min interview. We assess both your output and how you think in real time. The exercise will be relevant to your role (e.g. analysis, strategy, or process design).

    • For engineering roles: A 90-min live technical interview on CoderPad covering code understanding, review, system design, and product thinking (with AI serving as a collaboration tool).

  4. Step 3 – Leadership interview (45 min): Conversation with a SteerCo member and a Founder.

  5. References: Up to 3 calls with former colleagues or managers.

☕ You may also be invited for coffee with team members to get a feel for our culture.

Compensation: €41.2K – €79.8K • Offers Equity

title: Optical Engineer (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
Focused Energy is a fusion energy startup with the goal of generating unlimited clean energy to responsibly meet future global demand. With the use and commercialization of laser-induced inertial fusion, a clean and highly efficient power generation technology is coming within reach, suitable to ensure a secure and scalable future energy supply.

We are seeking a skilled and driven Optical Engineer to design, analyze, and help realize the next generation of high-energy and high-average-power laser systems that underpin Focused Energy’s fusion program. In this role, you will be responsible for turning advanced optical concepts into robust, manufacturable, and operable experimental and production laser systems.

Your work will directly enable the performance, stability, and scalability of our fusion laser infrastructure — ensuring that optical designs meet extreme power, precision, and reliability requirements while remaining practical to build, integrate, and operate.

What you’ll do

  • Optical System Design: Design, model, and optimize complex optical systems for high-energy and high-average-power laser applications, balancing performance, robustness, and manufacturability.

  • Simulation & Analysis: Use advanced optical modeling tools (e.g., Zemax / OpticStudio) to perform ray tracing, tolerance analysis, stray light analysis, and wavefront propagation to predict and validate system behavior.

  • Performance Specification: Define detailed optical specifications including component selection, materials, coatings, and tolerances to meet demanding power, fluence, and stability requirements.

  • Integration & Commissioning: Partner closely with technicians, laser engineers, and mechanical and electrical teams during assembly, alignment, testing, and commissioning of optical systems, troubleshooting issues as they arise.

  • System Optimization: Identify and resolve performance limitations related to aberrations, thermal effects, alignment sensitivity, and stray light to ensure stable, repeatable operation at high power.

  • Documentation & Communication: Produce high-quality technical documentation, analyses, and design reviews to support internal development, knowledge sharing, and external collaboration.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work across disciplines to ensure optical designs integrate cleanly into larger laser, mechanical, electrical, vacuum, and control system architectures.

Who you are

  • A degree in Optical Engineering, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, with professional experience designing and analyzing optical systems for laser or photonics applications.

  • Deep hands-on experience with Zemax (OpticStudio) or comparable optical design and simulation tools, including tolerance and stray light analysis.

  • Strong understanding of classical optics, Gaussian beam propagation, laser physics, and material behavior under high-intensity or high-fluence conditions.

  • Comfortable moving between modeling and the lab — supporting alignment, testing, debugging, and iteration of real optical hardware.

  • You bring rigor to your designs, anticipate failure modes, and care deeply about accuracy, documentation, and long-term reliability.

  • You can work effectively with scientists, engineers, and technicians and communicate complex optical concepts clearly across disciplines.

  • Preferred: Experience with MATLAB, Python, or similar tools for analysis, modeling, or automation of design workflows.

  • Preferred: Familiarity with cleanroom practices, vacuum-compatible optical design, large-aperture optics, or advanced components such as adaptive or deformable optics.


Focused Energy is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive environment. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Focused Energy will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, benefits.

title: Partnership Manager - Accountant Sector
descriptionHtml:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

We are looking for an experienced Partnership Manager to join our Accountant Partnerships team in France, specifically focused on building and developing relationships with accounting firms and accountant networks.

The core purpose of this role is to turn accounting firms into long-term Alan partners and advocates. You will help them recommend Alan to their clients, improve their day-to-day experience with health insurance and payroll administration, and generate qualified business opportunities for Alan’s Sales teams.

The accountant ecosystem represents a significant growth opportunity for Alan. France has approximately 22,000 accounting firms supporting around 3.5 million companies, and Alan’s existing Accountant Partnership channel has already generated significant ARR through a relatively small number of partners.

The team is now entering a new phase of development. We are hiring new Partnership Manager to help build a scalable, high-performing partner network and contribute to Alan’s ambition to make Accountant Partnerships a strategic growth channel.

Here is how your key outcomes will look like:

  1. Build and grow a strong partner network: Identify, prioritise and develop relationships with high-potential accounting firms and networks.

  2. Drive partnerships from discussion to activation: Lead partnership discussions, onboarding and launch, ensuring that Alan creates value for both accountants and their clients.

  3. Activate partners and generate business opportunities: Build engagement plans, support partner enablement and work closely with Sales to turn recommendations into qualified opportunities.

  4. Help scale the Accountant Partnerships model: Manage partner performance, share insights with internal teams and contribute to the development of scalable playbooks, tools and processes.

⭐ Is it you we’re looking for?

We’re looking for someone who combines strong partnership and commercial skills with the ability to build trusted relationships in a complex and evolving B2B ecosystem.

The ideal candidate will be comfortable managing partnerships from initial contact to activation and long-term development. They should enjoy working autonomously in an environment where there is still a lot to build.

You may be a great fit at Alan if you have/are:

  • 5+ years of experience in partnerships, business development, account management or customer success in a B2B environment

  • Experience managing partnerships throughout the full lifecycle, from prospecting and closing to activation and ongoing relationship management

  • Experience managing a portfolio of partners, ideally in a fast-growing company

  • Strong negotiation, communication, presentation and relationship-building skills

  • A data-oriented mindset, with the ability to track performance and prioritise opportunities

  • The ability to collaborate effectively with Sales, Marketing, Product, Data and Operations teams

  • An entrepreneurial mindset, strong ownership and the ability to work autonomously

  • Full professional fluency in French and professional fluency in English

Experience working directly with accounting firms, payroll providers, HR software or insurance companies would be a strong plus.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have experience with B2B distribution partnerships, where a third party recommends or distributes a solution to its own customers. Experience limited to technology integrations, co-marketing or visibility partnerships would be less relevant for this role.

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the C0-D level.

Everything else is a plus. We care about having a diversity of experiences, profiles and backgrounds in our team.

🙌 Perks & Benefits

At Alan, we believe that being in good health is a basic need, and it starts with our employees. This is why Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

Therefore, we offer:

  • Fair rewards. Generous equity packages complement your base salary, for permanent contracts only.

  • Flexible office with hybrid setup. Amazing office space at our Paris HQ or sponsored co-working hubs in Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes or Biarritz.

  • All the tools you need. Top of the range equipment: Macbook Air, keyboard, laptop stand, monitor, and Bose noise-canceling headphones.

  • Flexible vacation policy and flexible working hours. Organize your time as you wish.

  • Delightful healthcare insurance: Extremely comprehensive health insurance - 100% for you and your children, 90-100% for partners depending on your country (permanent contracts only).

  • Transport. Generous transit benefit

  • Learning & Training opportunities. A highly flexible training policy free books and budget to attend and speak at conferences if the opportunity arises.

  • Personal growth through coaching: At Alan, coaching isn't just a perk - it's core to who we are. Every Alaner is paired with a dedicated coach from day one, who helps maximize their impact, nurture engagement, and navigate Alan's values to develop their full potential. Learn more about our coaching culture.

  • Parental leave. Extended parental leave for all new parents, for permanent contracts only.

Important note: we hire people not roles.

After reading this job description, if you feel like you don’t have all the necessary prerequisites but that it matches where you are now or what you'd like to grow into in your next position, we encourage you to apply!

Not everybody will enter our recruitment process, but all, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply as it can only bring learnings or success.

🔖 Check out our About Alan and Career pages, as well as our Medium, blog and Glassdoor page for more info.#LI-DNP

title: People AI & Automation Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Join Pigment: The AI Platform Redefining Business Planning Pigment is the AI-powered business planning and performance management platform built for agility and scale. We connect people, data, and processes in one intuitive platform, with AI agents that work alongside every team, from Finance to HR, to build, adapt, and align strategic plans in real time.

Founded in 2019, Pigment is one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies globally, passing $100M in ARR in 2026 and doubling revenue for the second year in a row. Industry leaders like Unilever, Uber, Anthropic, Snowflake, and Siemens use Pigment every day to make better-informed decisions and navigate any scenario with confidence.

In October 2026, we raised a $250M Series E at a $2.3B valuation, bringing our total funding to $650M+. Today we’re a growing team of 700+ across Paris, London, New York, Toronto, San Francisco, and Austin, and we’ve been named a Visionary in the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Financial Planning Software two years running.

At Pigment, we take smart risks, celebrate bold ideas, and challenge the status quo - all while working as one team. If you’re driven by innovation and ready to make an impact at scale, we’d love to hear from you.

What you will do

1. Build and run automations with AI

  • Automate the employee lifecycle: build, test, deploy and maintain workflows for recruiting-to-onboarding handoffs, employee changes, learning administration and offboarding.

  • Connect the People stack: move data reliably between Pigment and the other People tools (performance, learning, ticketing), using various automation tools, APIs and webhooks.

  • Translate process into logic: sit with People process owners, map how work happens today, and turn it into clean workflows with triggers, conditions, approvals, notifications and error handling.

  • Handle failure safely: design for missing data, unavailable systems and unexpected inputs, and route exceptions to the right owner instead of failing silently.

  • Run what you ship: monitor production workflows, investigate failures and fix recurring issues at the root, and align with the Data & Automation team.

2. Build AI agents and self-service

  • Build People agents: use LLMs and Pigment's native AI capabilities to build agents that answer employee and manager questions, draft responses and route tickets.

  • Prompt and evaluate: write prompts and agent instructions, build test cases, and measure answer accuracy, source quality and appropriate escalation. Keep a versioned library of approved prompts and results.

  • Connect approved knowledge only: link agents to the right sources for each audience, and make sure sensitive or unresolved questions go to a person.

  • Test the market: pilot new AI features and tools, and move them to production when relevant.

  • Spot new opportunities: bring workflow and agent ideas from People teams to the People Strategy & Tech Lead, with a first view of effort and value.

3. Document, monitor and improve

  • Treat People workflow like product code: keep clear documentation, schemas and runbooks for every workflow and agent: purpose, dependencies, logic, owner, monitoring and change history.

  • Keep an inventory: maintain an up-to-date list of the automations, agents, integrations and prompts you support, and retire what no longer works.

  • Measure service health: track success rate, processing time, answer quality, escalation rate and incidents, and report them to the People Strategy & Tech Lead regularly.

  • Apply responsible AI controls: implement the access, data and human-review requirements defined by Security, Privacy and Legal, and re-test after any model, data or configuration change.

  • Support adoption: write short guides and release notes, and help People teams use what you build.

  • Work within company standards: build with the stack and follow the IT and security guidelines set by the Data & Automation team, and document your work so others can support it when you are away.

Who you are

  • Experience: 2+ years in AI implementations, automations, data or a similar role, ideally in a fast-growing tech or SaaS company. No HR background needed: what matters is that you have built something real that others rely on, and that you want to turn People into an AI-powered team. Internships and apprenticeships count if you ship real things.

  • The builder mindset: you have built workflows or integrations that other people actually use, with tools such as n8n, Zapier, Make, Workato or Power Automate. Scripting (SQL, Python or JavaScript) or expert-level spreadsheet logic is a strong plus.

  • AI-fluent: you know how to prompt LLMs, you have built or tested an agent or an AI assistant, and you are excited to replace repetitive human steps with reliable automation.

  • Systems thinking: you understand APIs, webhooks, structured data, permissions and conditional logic, and you know how automated services fail.

  • People curiosity: you understand or you are interested in core HR processes (hiring, onboarding, internal mobility, offboarding, payroll inputs) and can turn a process owner's needs into system logic.

  • Judgment with sensitive data: you have worked with sensitive or confidential information (financial, legal, customer or personal data) and handle it with care, and you know when a human must stay in the loop.

  • Clear communicator: you explain technical choices and trade-offs to non-technical partners, and you document as you go.

  • Education: degree in engineering, data, information systems, business school with a focus on BI or information systems. Self-taught builders with strong evidence of work are welcome.

  • Fluency in English.

Nice to have

  • Experience automating or deploying AI inside an HR or People team.

  • Hands-on time with HiBob, Lever or similar HRIS and ATS tools, or with a ticketing and knowledge-base tool.

  • Familiarity with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agent evaluation or AI-assisted development tools.

  • Experience working with Security, Privacy or Legal teams, or knowledge of GDPR and responsible AI in employment processes.


What success looks like in the first 12 months

  • Priority automations live in production, each with a measurable drop in manual work, processing time or errors.

  • Self-service agent launched with tested answer quality, approved sources and clear escalation paths.

  • A versioned library of prompts, test cases and evaluation results for approved People use cases.

  • Monitoring, documentation and runbooks in place for every workflow and agent you support.

  • Automated data-quality checks catching missing, late or inconsistent data and routing it to an owner.

  • A regular service-health view for the People Strategy & Tech Lead: success rate, incidents, adoption and open improvements.

title: Placement Agentic Software Engineer - 2027
descriptionHtml:
Join Instil’s agentic product development team for your placement year and learn to build software the way it will be built in the agentic age: engineers owning the problem, the architecture and the key decisions, with AI agents accelerating everything in between.

About the role

At Instil, agentic product engineering is how we deliver. Our teams work alongside an agentic workforce that generates requirements, builds across parallel workstreams, runs continuous quality and security checks or monitoring systems in production. The result is software that ships faster, with lower risk.

The agents do a lot, but people stay firmly in charge - orchestrating. We own the problem, the architecture and the key decisions. That is the skill set we will help you build from day one.

As a placement student you will join a delivery team working on real client products for organisations ranging from ambitious start-ups to global brands. You will learn the fundamentals of great software engineering and, alongside them, how to direct, review and get the best out of AI agents.

What you'll do

You will work across our full delivery lifecycle, supported by experienced engineers and mentors.

  1. Plan: take part in discovery with clients, help shape requirements and use agents to turn ideas into rapid prototypes and a backlog ready to build.

  2. Build: write, review and test production code, directing agents across parallel workstreams and learning to judge when their output is right and when it is not.

  3. Ship: help release software to production, design for observability and use agents to monitor systems, analyse issues and drive improvements.

Along the way you will:

  • Learn to make sound technical decisions and explain them clearly

  • Build good habits in security, testing and code quality, so speed never comes at the cost of trust

  • Work directly with clients and colleagues as part of a collaborative, multi-disciplinary team

  • Share what you learn, as our ways of working with agents are evolving all the time

What we're looking for

We care more about how you think than what you already know.

Essential:

  • Currently studying towards a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related discipline, with a placement year as part of your programme

  • Solid programming fundamentals in at least one modern language, such as TypeScript, Python, Java, Kotlin, or C#

  • Hands-on experience with AI coding tools, Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor or similar, through projects, hackathons or coursework

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the judgement to question an answer rather than simply accept it

  • Clear communication skills and an enjoyment of working in a team

Nice to have:

  • Side projects, open source contributions or a portfolio that shows what you have built

What you'll get

  • A structured placement programme combining engineering fundamentals with hands-on training in agentic development

  • A mentor and regular feedback throughout your year

  • Real client work from your first weeks, not just internal projects

  • Access to the latest AI tools and the time to learn them properly

  • A collaborative culture where people share knowledge openly

Why Join Instil?

At Instil, we believe great work starts with happy, motivated people. That’s why we’ve built a benefits package that supports your wellbeing, growth, and life outside of work, because when you thrive, so do we.

  • Recognition That Matters: A discretionary annual performance bonus that rewards your impact and contribution to our success.

  • Financial Security: A highly competitive pension scheme with generous employer contributions, private healthcare, and life assurance for peace of mind.

  • Health & Wellbeing: Employee Assistance Programme, mental health support, cycle-to-work scheme, and regular social events to keep our culture vibrant.

title: Platform Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About us

We love pets - which is why we’re on a mission to make the world a better place for pets and their parents.  We offer pet insurance policies with generous pet health benefits that are designed with their needs in mind. We’ve helped half a million pets stay happy and healthy since 2017 - and many more customers throughout the world are joining us every day.  Our company is respectful, fun-loving and passionate about pets and their wellbeing.  Throughout our business you'll meet people who think differently, aim for impact, and love to try new things.  Want to join our pack?  Join us. Love every moment. Love ManyPets.

A day in the life

As a Platform Engineer, you will initially join our platform squad. We build and maintain the AWS infrastructure, deployment pipelines, tooling and engineering standards that every other squad at ManyPets depends on.

This role has a strong security focus, and it will become more security focused over time. Much of the work is compliance and assurance: building and running the tooling that checks our cloud estate against our security standards, writing the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one, gathering the evidence we need for ISO 27001 and our other obligations, and supporting the audits that depend on it. Alongside that you will help us tighten access controls across our cloud estate, and take on ownership of the edge and network security tooling that protects our services.

Over time this role moves across to work directly with our Head of Security as we build out a dedicated security function at ManyPets. You will help shape what that function does and how it works, rather than inheriting something already built.

Our environment is fast-paced and highly collaborative. You will work closely with your teammates using pair or mob programming, participating in regular workshops and planning sessions, primarily over Zoom, with occasional in-person collaboration.

We embrace modern development practices:

· All our services are cloud-hosted on AWS, using serverless and event-driven architectures for scalability and resilience.

· We use a fully automated deployment pipeline, allowing you to release to production within minutes, multiple times per day.

· We define our infrastructure as code, and we emphasise observability, testing and secure-by-design principles from the start.

As a squad we own our work end-to-end, including development, maintenance and support. You will play a key role in ensuring the reliability and quality of what we provide to the rest of engineering, and contribute to a culture of rapid learning and continuous improvement.

Your responsibilities

ü Build and maintain secure platform foundations

o Design, build and maintain the shared cloud infrastructure, tooling and deployment pipelines that other squads rely on.

o Define infrastructure as code so our environments are consistent, repeatable and reviewable.

o Make secure configuration the default, so squads get it without having to ask for it.

o Maintain the edge and network security tooling that protects our services.

o Share in the day-to-day operational ownership of the platform, responding to requests and issues raised by other squads.

Make our security posture measurable

o Automate the gathering of evidence for ISO 27001 and our other compliance obligations, so that an audit means pulling a report rather than running a manual exercise.

o Write the scripts and small services that turn a manual security check into a scheduled, repeatable one.

o Triage findings from our scanning and posture tooling such as Aikido and Ascidian, work out which ones actually matter, and either fix them or get them in front of the team that can.

o Work with our Head of Security to turn written policy into controls that are enforced by tooling.

Strengthen access and identity controls

o Review and tighten access across our cloud accounts, working towards least privilege.

o Improve how we manage secrets, credentials and machine identities.

o Make access changes auditable, and straightforward for engineers to request and for us to review.

Extend our platform standards beyond AWS

o Help us apply the standards, tooling and controls we have built in AWS to our Google Cloud estate.

o Work with the teams who use Google Cloud to understand their needs and where the gaps are.

Team collaboration

o Work closely with other squad members and stakeholders to align on goals and solutions.

o Support engineers across other squads who use our platform, and take their feedback seriously.

o Proactively build shared understanding across the team through pairing, discussions, and reviews.

o Document your work clearly to support knowledge sharing and future maintenance.

Self development

o Take ownership of your learning journey and technical development plan.

o Approach challenges with curiosity and a growth mindset.

o Learn from your peers and actively seek feedback and mentorship.

Your skills and experience

We are looking for someone with:

· Commercial experience building and maintaining cloud infrastructure on a major cloud provider (AWS, Google Cloud or Azure).

· Hands-on experience defining infrastructure as code.

· Experience building and maintaining continuous integration and deployment pipelines.

· A good working understanding of cloud security fundamentals.

· Proficiency in at least one scripting language, ideally Python.

· Comfort working in a regulated environment. We are FCA regulated and take our ISO 27001 commitments seriously.

You will also need at least one current associate-level cloud certification:

· AWS: Solutions Architect Associate, Developer Associate or SysOps Administrator Associate. We would also be interested in the AWS Certified Security Speciality.

· Google Cloud: Associate Cloud Engineer.

· Microsoft Azure: Administrator Associate (AZ-104) or Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500).

Entry-level certifications such as AWS Cloud Practitioner, Google Cloud Digital Leader and Azure Fundamentals do not meet this on their own. Please include the certification name and your credential ID or badge link with your application.

We would also like to see at least one of the following. You do not need both, and we will support you to build the other:

· A security specialism, where you can tell us about security or compliance tooling you have built and what it caught.

· Experience across more than one cloud provider, ideally both AWS and Google Cloud.

The interview process

This position has a four-stage interview process, which will be held via Zoom.

· Stage 1 - an initial conversation with a member of our Talent team.

· Stage 2 - an informal meeting with the hiring manager for about 45 minutes. We will explain more about the role and explore how your experience matches up with what we need.

· Stage 3 - a longer interview, up to an hour, with the hiring manager and two engineers from the team. We will ask some competency questions and work through a technical scenario together. There is no take-home exercise.

· Stage 4 - an informal conversation with our Head of Security.

About the team

The EPD ("Engineering, Product and Design") team operates with a squad system and Agile ways of working within quarterly terms - and we really enjoy working collaboratively. We hold regular ‘Hack Weeks’ to look at products and address problems relating to the business, and we get the chance to highlight and work on things we’re interested in and feel passionately about.

Our tech stack

We are on a mission to become the best we can be, constantly challenging ourselves to achieve and learn. You will be supported to learn new technology – both in breadth and depth - and encouraged to challenge our ways of thinking with new and innovative ideas.

Our “north star” is to become an elite performer as defined by the 4 key DORA metrics. To drive towards elite status, we apply and continually inspect and adapt the best Agile frameworks and practices inspired by DevOps, SRE, Scrum, XP and Lean. We are a highly collaborative environment and regularly practice Mob and Pair based programming which we believe improve our quality of delivery and share understanding.

We take our operational performance, security, and reliability as seriously as our quality and development practices. We are cloud hosted and highly automated, primarily on AWS with some critical services running on Google Cloud.

Some specific technologies we use include: AWS | Google Cloud | Python | MongoDB | Aikido | Ascidian | Cloudflare

Salary range:£55,000—£65,000 GBP

Ways of working

On a typical day you’ll be working from a laptop with a screen, mouse, keyboard, and headset.  You’ll be meeting your colleagues on Zoom and keeping in touch regularly via email and Slack too – we’d expect you to be using your computer for around seven hours a day.  We’d ask that you have a distraction-free work area and a reliable internet connection with a speed of 25Mbps so you can work effectively.  We’ll make sure you have the right home set-up that supports you in the role by providing best-in-class technology, money towards a desk, and vision support.

Inclusion at ManyPets

We promise to give you the same opportunities as everyone else and we won’t discriminate against you at any point in the process. This includes how we source talent, our interview process, our conditions of employment (including pay) and feedback.  If you'd like to read more about this, please download our Approach to Inclusion policy. 

Reasonable adjustments and support

If you need any help, support, or advice at any point during the hiring process please email
