title: Senior Nuclear Theorist - Few-Body Physics (gn) @ Fusion Energy Venture, Munich
descriptionHtml:
This is an Atlantic portfolio venture.

About the Venture

Snap Fusion develops a fundamentally new approach to controlled fusion energy.

We are a small team of physicists and engineers. The work is early, the questions are real, and the standard is high. Our findings feed into research in fusion energy, scientific discovery, advanced simulation, AI for Physics and quantum technologies.

Some problems are too important not to solve.

Your mission
Lead the nuclear theory behind a new approach to fusion energy.

At Snap Fusion, we are pursuing a bold mission: developing a fundamentally new approach to controlled fusion energy.

Parts of our roadmap rest on questions of low-energy nuclear physics. Some of these have clear answers in the literature; others turn out, on close reading, to be less settled than they first appear. Knowing which is which matters to us, because it shapes what we build and what we test.

We are therefore establishing an in-house nuclear theory effort, and we are looking for a senior few-body theorist to lead it. Your job will be to decide which of our questions current theory can actually answer, to answer those at a standard that would hold up to expert review, and to say plainly where the uncertainties lie.

This is an unusual setting for a theorist, in a good way: the questions are concrete, the team is small, and your conclusions will be acted on.

What you will do

You will work directly with the founders as theory lead. Your responsibilities may include:

• Leading theory projects from problem definition to a clear recommendation

• Judging which questions current nuclear theory can answer, and with what uncertainty

• Carrying out and supervising few-body scattering and reaction calculations

• Setting the benchmarks and cross-checks against which results are accepted

• Working with our computational physics lead on the numerical implementation of the methods you specify

• Reviewing theoretical and experimental claims that bear on our roadmap

• Building collaborations with academic groups, including for independent confirmation of key results

• Helping the rest of the team understand the physics behind your conclusions

Your assessments will directly inform Snap Fusion's technology roadmap.

What we’re looking for

You will probably hold a PhD in theoretical nuclear physics or a closely related field, with research experience beyond it. Ideal candidates will have strong experience in several of the following areas:

Nuclear theory

• Quantum scattering and reaction theory

• Few-body or ab initio methods

• Realistic nuclear interactions

• Resonances, thresholds, and continuum physics

• Low-energy charged-particle reactions

• Fusion cross sections and astrophysical S-factors

Scientific leadership. You should be comfortable:

• Running a research program with milestones and honest go/no-go decisions

• Saying that a question cannot be answered with current theory, when it cannot

• Writing clearly for readers who are not few-body specialists

• Reviewing other people's derivations, and having your own reviewed

Like most few-body theorists, you will have done a good deal of numerical work, and that experience will be valuable here. But this is a physics role first: we have a computational physics lead, and implementation is a collaboration rather than the core of your job.

Industry experience is not required.

Bonus Points

Experience with any of the following is a plus:

• Light-nuclei reaction calculations

• R-matrix or related continuum methods

• Nuclear astrophysics

• Benchmark comparisons between methods or codes

• Close collaboration with experimentalists

• Refereeing and reviewing

• Teaching or mentoring

Who thrives here?

You may be a great fit if:

descriptionHtml:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the Role:

We are looking for a strategic and results-driven Senior Partner Account Executive to launch, scale, and optimise partnerships across our ecosystem with a focus on insurance carriers and brokers. Samsara's telematics and dashcam technology already help thousands of customers improve safety and reduce risk - this role will accelerate those benefits by developing high-impact partnerships that drive mutual growth.

You will be the face of Samsara to insurance executives, building scalable programmes that directly influence customer acquisition, retention, and loss cost improvement. If you thrive in fast-paced, high-growth environments, are motivated by measurable business impact, and enjoy turning ideas into reality, this is your opportunity to make a difference.

Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

In this role you will:

  • Own and grow our relationships with insurance carriers, brokers and MGAs in the UK
  • Design and run partner programmes that drive customer acquisition, retention and loss-cost improvement - and the Samsara revenue that comes with them
  • Map accounts with partners, pick joint targets and bring Samsara sales into the deals
  • Build the playbook: how we qualify, onboard and scale insurance partnerships

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact - helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your partners are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live. Samsara's top employees do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
  • You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you'll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
  • You want to develop the playbook, not just follow one: Our partner ecosystem is young. You'll define how we take partners to value - from first conversation to joint customers - and build the model that lets those partnerships deliver maximum value for Samsara at scale.
  • You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
  • You build genuine relationships with your partners and our customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven't been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara's high-performance culture means you'll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • Strong sales, partnerships, or business development experience, ideally within a B2B technology or insurance-related field and a track record of overachievement.
  • A builder mentality - you thrive in ambiguous environments and know how to create structure, process, and scale.

An ideal candidate also has:

Why Join Samsara?

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

About us

We love pets - which is why we’re on a mission to make the world a better place for pets and their parents.  We offer pet insurance policies with generous pet health benefits that are designed with their needs in mind. We’ve helped half a million pets stay happy and healthy since 2017 - and many more customers throughout the world are joining us every day.  Our company is respectful, fun-loving and passionate about pets and their wellbeing.  Throughout our business you'll meet people who think differently, aim for impact, and love to try new things.  Want to join our pack?  Join us. Love every moment. Love ManyPets.

Role and purpose mandate

ManyPets is continuing to evolve as it scales, with increasing organisational complexity and a need for strong People partnership that enables leaders to build high-performing, engaged and effective teams.

The Senior People Advisor plays a critical role in aligning people priorities with business goals, partnering with senior leaders to shape organisational capability, improve performance, strengthen manager capability and support sustainable growth.

This role combines advisory partnership with practical delivery across organisational effectiveness, employee relations, workforce planning, leadership capability, engagement, wellbeing and data-led decision making.

You will partner closely with designated senior leaders and management teams to deliver effective people plans and solutions, ensuring they land well, are embedded within the teams you support, and contribute directly to business performance, employee experience and our values-led culture.

A day in the life

  • Accountable for providing employee relations advise to designated business areas, supporting leaders with organisational design, workforce planning, performance, engagement and complex people matters.
  • Provide hands-on support, coaching leaders through ambiguity and ensuring People activity is commercially grounded, legally sound and aligned to company priorities.
  • Support People Advisors, ensuring consistent, high-quality advice and operational delivery across the employee lifecycle.

Your responsibilities

People Partnership

  • Partner with senior leaders to translate business priorities into clear, practical and measurable people plans.
  • Provide trusted advice on organisational change, leadership effectiveness, team health, engagement, performance and culture.
  • Use people data, engagement insight and employee relations trends to identify risks, opportunities and areas for action.
  • Coach leaders to make balanced, inclusive and commercially grounded people decisions.
  • Ensure a values-led People experience is felt by teams and delivered in line with business priorities.

Change Management & Engagement

  • Diagnose and lead the People elements of change projects that improve business performance and align with strategic goals.
  • Partner with leaders and managers to ensure change is understood, communicated effectively and embedded well.
  • Support change initiatives including organisational design, redeployment, ways-of-working changes and team restructures, ensuring risks are identified and mitigated.
  • Work with senior leaders on timely communication and engagement plans for upcoming change.

Employee Relations, Risk & Performance

  • Lead on complex employee relations matters, ensuring fair, consistent, legally sound and values-led outcomes.

Data, Reward & Governance

Why this role matters

About you

  • Proven experience as a People Advisor, ideally in a fast-paced, scaling, operational or customer-service-led environment.

title: Senior People Partner
descriptionHtml:
Senior People Partner

Cloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000

Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function.

THE MOMENT

Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago.

You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them.

This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one.

WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT

In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty.

  • Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back.

  • People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding.

  • Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning.

  • CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to.

To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one.

THE ROLE

You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job:

  • Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish.

  • Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs.

  • Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate.

When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day.

WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS

New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today.

Yours

  • The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end.

  • Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding.

  • Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems.

  • Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027):

    • Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago.

    • Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation.

    • Background screening in Zinc.

    • Security clearance coordination.

    • Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting.

    • Our working groups and committees.

  • Once the People Partner joins:

    • A structured handover of the operational core.

    • Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner.

Shared

  • Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that.

  • Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join.

Not yours

  • Recruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition.

  • The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO.

  • Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO.

THE STACK

  • Rippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives.

  • Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that.

  • Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for.

  • Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative.

  • Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over.

  • Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done.

  • Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go.

  • Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against.

  • Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook.

  • Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome.

  • Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHS

  • You’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them.

  • At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you.

  • Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over.

  • You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land.

  • Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point.

  • You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up.

  • The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • Deep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome.

  • A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to.

  • Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work.

  • Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to.

  • Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards.

  • Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up.

  • Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory.

THE HONEST PART

This role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title.

You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows.

This probably isn’t for you if you want a formal team from day one, or if you’d rather leave payroll and onboarding to someone else. It probably is for you if you want to prove you can run this function well enough, top to bottom, that a team gets built around you.

If that sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, let’s talk.

title: Senior Performance Marketing Manager für Meta & Google Ads (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Deine Mission

Kurz vorab: Diese Stelle richtet sich an Leute mit echter Erfahrung. Du steuerst seit mindestens drei Jahren eigenverantwortlich Werbebudgets auf Meta und Google und hast zuletzt mindestens 50.000 Euro im Monat selbst verantwortet. Wenn das auf dich zutrifft und du Lust auf Tempo und Verantwortung hast, bist du hier richtig. Wir arbeiten gemeinsam im Office im Herzen Münchens, weil wir im Team am schnellsten sind.

Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für die Performance unserer Kunden auf Meta und Google. Du entscheidest, wohin das Budget geht, was getestet wird und was skaliert. Du liest Zahlen so, dass du die Ursache findest und nicht nur das Symptom. Und du erklärst Kunden klar, was passiert und was als Nächstes kommt.

Konkret

  • Du steuerst Meta- und Google-Ads-Konten für E-Commerce- und Leadgen-Brands, von der Struktur bis zur Skalierung.
  • Du planst Budgets und Tests und entscheidest nach Profitabilität, nicht nur nach ROAS.
  • Du arbeitest eng mit unserem Creative-Team und sagst, welche Creatives deine Konten als Nächstes brauchen.
  • Du behältst Tracking und Datenqualität im Blick: Conversions API, Enhanced Conversions und GA4.
  • Du führst Kundengespräche auf Augenhöhe, auch wenn die Zahlen mal schlecht sind.
  • Du nutzt AI-Tools für Analyse, Reporting und Routine und gibst dein Wissen im Team weiter.

Dein Profil

  • Mindestens 3 Jahre Erfahrung in der eigenverantwortlichen Steuerung von Meta und Google Ads.
  • Du hast zuletzt Monatsbudgets ab 50.000 Euro selbst verantwortet.
  • Du kennst E-Commerce- oder Leadgen-Konten aus der Praxis und kannst konkrete Ergebnisse nennen.
  • Du verstehst Attribution, Tracking und Unit Economics gut genug, um Zahlen zu hinterfragen.
  • Du kommunizierst klar, mit Kunden und im Team.
  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse, weil du mit unseren Kunden sprichst.
  • Du wohnst in München oder ziehst für den Job her. Wir arbeiten gemeinsam im Office.

Diese Rolle ist für dich, wenn

  • du Verantwortung für Ergebnisse willst und nicht nur für Aufgaben.
  • du Entscheidungen mit Zahlen begründest.
  • du im Team besser wirst und andere besser machst.
  • du neugierig auf AI bist und sie im Alltag einsetzt.

Noch nicht passend ist die Rolle, wenn

  • du gerade erst ins Performance Marketing einsteigst.
  • du Kampagnen bisher vor allem nach Vorgabe umgesetzt hast.

Nice-to-have

  • Erfahrung mit TikTok oder Pinterest Ads.
  • Erfahrung mit Shopify, Klaviyo oder serverseitigem Tracking.
  • Agenturerfahrung mit mehreren Kunden gleichzeitig.

Warum wir?

  • Verantwortung ab dem ersten Tag: eigene Kunden, eigene Budgets, eigene Entscheidungen.
  • Ein starkes Creative-Team im Haus, das liefert, was deine Konten brauchen.
  • Eigene AI-Workflows für Analyse und Reporting, damit du Zeit für Strategie hast.
  • Motiviertes High-Performance-Team, keine Politik, flache Hierarchien.
  • Spannende E-Commerce- und Leadgen-Brands (Food, Beauty, Lifestyle).
  • Benefitpaket mit Sachbezug, Wellpass, Mittagessen und Deutschlandticket.
  • Modernes, zentrales Office am Gärtnerplatz in München.
  • Team-Events, Workshops und Weiterbildungen.

Darauf schauen wir

Ein Anschreiben brauchst du nicht. Wichtig sind uns dein Lebenslauf und deine Antworten im Bewerbungsformular. Dort fragen wir nach deiner Erfahrung, deinem Budget und einem Konto, das du selbst gesteuert hast. Antworte bitte mit Zahlen.

Wenn du dich über ein anderes Portal bewirbst, schreib diese drei Angaben bitte in deinen Lebenslauf: Jahre Erfahrung, zuletzt verantwortetes Monatsbudget und ein Konto mit Ergebnis.

So geht es danach weiter: Videocall, eine kurze Case-Aufgabe, ein Probetag bei uns im Office mit persönlichem Gespräch, dann unsere Entscheidung.

title: Senior Product Designer EMEA
descriptionHtml:
WunderGraph is a fast-growing startup, our goal is to bring everybody together to build digital products end-to-end. From interface design to API implementation, we provide the platform to go from sketch to product in a category-defining collaborative experience. Our North Star is to take the friction out of bringing digital ideas to life, making room for your ideas and productivity.

Developers from some of the biggest companies in the world are using WunderGraph to design and streamline their API environments. We raised our Series A ($7.5 million USD) in March 2025, being backed by eBay, Karma Ventures, and Aspenwood Ventures.

The culture we are creating together is extremely important to us. Read here how we are Building the Company We Always Wanted to Work In.

We invite everyone that wants to join us to understand our Core Beliefs and if you want to make an impact, have your voice heard, and work in a no-BS organization where you can get stuff done, look no further and apply today so we can chat.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Product Designer at WunderGraph, you are the connection between what our users will find most helpful and what our engineers build. Considering the users also happen to be other developers, this becomes an interesting challenge to think about the Developer Experience as the User Experience. You combine sharp user insight, craft, and pragmatism to deliver experiences that are elegant, usable, and built to scale.

This is a wide-reaching role, as design roles at a startup should be. One week you might be running user interviews to shape a new feature; the next, refining our design system or designing a marketing landing page. You ground your work in evidence rather than assumption, partner closely with product and engineering, and turn what you learn about users into a clear, informed UX strategy that guides where we go next.

TEAM INTEGRATION

  • Reports to the VP of Product; is part of the Product team

  • Aligns closely with the CEO (Product) and Head of Customer Success (customer experience and business impact)

  • Collaborate within the Product team with the Delivery Lead and the Design Engineer

  • Collaborates cross-functionally with engineering, marketing, product, and customer success

ROLE OBJECTIVES

You are successful if you:

  • Take ownership of the complete design lifecycle, bridging the gap between initial discovery and final delivery for web and product interfaces.

  • Cultivate an evidence-based UX strategy that leverages user research and data to steer the product's evolution.

  • Oversee the growth of a unified and extensible design system that spans both our product and marketing efforts.

  • Convert user insights and organizational objectives into pragmatic, human-centric solutions engineered for long-term scalability.

  • Advocate for excellence in accessibility, responsiveness, and performance as fundamental pillars of your craft.

  • Provide mentorship to the team, sharing expertise in research methodologies and design principles.

  • Refine the visual and functional identity of WunderGraph through meticulous and high-impact design work.

  • Impact high-level product strategy by demonstrating how user-focused decisions drive tangible business impact.

ROLE TASKS

The role focuses on, but is not limited to:

Product Design

  • Design and prototype user flows, interfaces, and interactions with scalability in mind.

  • Own design problems end to end. From initial concept through execution and iteration after launch.

  • Rapidly produce wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity designs, exploring multiple concepts and iterating quickly.

  • Define and evolve our design system and component library, keeping it consistent and maintainable.

  • Partner closely with engineers on feasibility, quality, and handoff, contributing to technical decisions (and coding where you're comfortable and it helps as a plus, not a requirement).

  • Introduce advanced prototyping, interaction design, and motion practices.

UX Research & Strategy

  • Plan and conduct user research across discovery and validation via user interviews, surveys, usability testing, and competitor analysis.

  • Turn ambiguous product questions into decision-grade research that maps to real product and design decisions.

  • Synthesize findings into clear insights, personas, journey maps, and opportunity areas that the team can act on.

  • Build and maintain a shared insight repository so learning is reusable, searchable, and available to everyone.

  • Translate research into an informed, evolving UX strategy that guides the roadmap and anchors design direction in real user needs.

  • Advocate for the user in prioritization and roadmap discussions, and define what "better" looks like through clear UX success metrics.

  • Run discovery workshops and share insights so research shows up where decisions are made like in design reviews, product planning, and standups embedding user knowledge from the get-go.

Web & Brand Experience

  • Own the design and evolution of WunderGraph's web presence.

  • Deliver assets that span product and marketing: landing pages, visuals, campaign graphics, and interactive components.

  • Shape and maintain a cohesive style guide, balancing design innovation with consistency.

  • Support brand storytelling with motion graphics and interactive elements.

ROLE REQUIREMENTS

  • Senior-level experience in Product Design or UX/UI Design, with a strong portfolio of shipped work.

  • Proven experience planning and running UX research (both generative and evaluative) and turning findings into strategy.

  • Proficiency in Figma, prototyping tools, and Adobe Creative Suite.

  • Strong background in UX and interaction design, accessibility, responsive design, and usability.

  • Experience contributing to or leading design systems and component libraries.

  • Comfortable using data and research to inform and defend design decisions.

  • Working knowledge of front-end technologies (HTML/CSS, JavaScript a plus) enough to collaborate closely with engineers.

  • Excellent communication, storytelling, and collaboration skills in English.

  • A self-starter who is comfortable with ambiguity and can lead initiatives independently in a fast-moving startup.

  • Comfortable working 100% remotely in a distributed team.

  • Willingness to travel occasionally for team retreats and workshops.

Why WunderGraph?

  • Work from wherever you thrive—we’re fully remote and globally distributed. If you're in Miami, come work with us in person! We also provide co-working space options worldwide if needed.

  • Pick your preferred work hardware

  • We focus on getting stuff done, and on having fun whilst doing so: work hard, play hard!

  • You can make a real difference and find lots of opportunities to grow together with us

  • Discretionary PTO: take the time you need to recharge

  • Competitive compensation

  • Depending on location, we offer healthcare benefits according to local standards

  • Team retreats across the globe

Note: This is a full-time, fully remote position, but we're prioritising candidates from EMEA. We are looking for someone who is available to work during European (CET) business hours.

The Process

We respect your time and interest in WunderGraph. This is why we're aiming to make the process as fast as possible. Here's what you can expect:

  • 30 min intro call with Mariya from our People team

  • 45 min discussion with the hiring manager. Following this, you might receive a small take home assignment related to the role. This is your chance to prove your skill!

  • Complete the assignment and review together with hiring manager

  • Meet the founders

  • Culture fit call with team members

  • Offer

Our process also includes reference and background checks. We aim to respond or provide feedback in 2 or 3 days between each stage of the process. We're usually hiring through Deel as our Employer of Record, except for Germany or Florida where we're hiring directly.

WunderGraph is an equal opportunity workplace; we welcome people from all backgrounds.

You can find out more about our ways of working together here:

WunderGraph Public Handbook and Resources

We’re looking forward to your application so we can grow together!

title: Senior Product Designer
descriptionHtml:
TransferGo is a growing fintech scale-up on a mission to champion financial freedom with care. We strive to provide tailored, more affordable financial services that make people's hard-earned money go further. Now in our 14th year, with close to 400 employees in offices across Europe and the UK, we’re crafting a brilliant, relevant product that makes a difference in people's lives and the well-being of their families. 

We’ve come this far by building a talented, diverse workforce on a fair culture and our strong values. Having this strong team of employees, we can serve those who really need our product to make their lives better. 

Join us as a Senior Product Designer and help shape how money moves across the globe 💸.

At TransferGo, Product Design is not simply a service that turns requirements into screens. Designers are part of the product trio, working alongside Product and Engineering to understand customer problems, shape strategy and deliver experiences that create meaningful customer and business outcomes.

In this role, you’ll lead complex initiatives from discovery through delivery across our web and mobile products. You’ll bring clarity to ambiguous problem spaces, connect customer needs with commercial and technical realities, and help teams make better product decisions.

You’ll also play an important role in raising the quality of design across TransferGo. Alongside owning your work, you’ll mentor other designers, contribute to our design practice and help us use emerging technologies, including AI to work more effectively without compromising judgement, responsibility or craft.

If you’re excited by complex fintech challenges, care deeply about the details and want to help a growing design team increase its impact, we’d love to meet you.

Here’s what you’ll do as a Senior Product Designer:

  • Lead significant product initiatives from problem framing and discovery through design, validation, delivery and post-launch iteration
  • Partner closely with Product Managers and Engineers to define the right problems, shape product direction and balance customer value, business goals and technical feasibility
  • Turn complex financial journeys and requirements into clear, accessible and trustworthy experiences across web and mobile
  • Use qualitative research, behavioural data, experimentation and product metrics to identify opportunities, evaluate trade-offs and measure the impact of your work
  • Plan and conduct appropriate research and validation, including user interviews, usability testing, concept testing and collaborative workshops
  • Develop and communicate a coherent design vision for your initiatives, connecting long-term direction with practical, iterative steps
  • Create high-quality user journeys, flows, wireframes, prototypes, interfaces and specifications, including edge cases and non-ideal states
  • Collaborate with Engineering early and throughout delivery, considering feasibility and ensuring the implemented experience meets the intended quality
  • Contribute to and evolve our design system, creating reusable patterns and improving consistency between design and production
  • Use AI-assisted tools thoughtfully throughout the design process; for example, to support research synthesis, problem framing, exploration, content design, rapid prototyping, data analysis and design reviews
  • Evaluate AI-generated work critically, protecting customer privacy and applying human judgement to accuracy, accessibility, quality and appropriateness
  • Communicate recommendations and design decisions clearly, using evidence and storytelling to build alignment and influence stakeholders
  • Mentor and support other designers through critique, feedback and practical guidance, helping raise the team’s overall quality and confidence
  • Improve the way we work by identifying opportunities to make design processes faster, clearer and more effective

You’ll report to our Head of Product Design.

What you’ll bring:

We don’t expect you to meet every single requirement listed. What matters most is your motivation, mindset and ability to learn. If you’re excited about this role and think you could be a great fit, we’d really like to hear from you.

  • 5+ years of experience designing and shipping digital products within cross-functional product teams
  • A strong portfolio demonstrating end-to-end ownership, strategic product thinking, polished UX/UI craft and measurable customer or business impact
  • A track record of independently leading complex initiatives from an ambiguous starting point through discovery, delivery and iteration
  • Strong product judgement and the ability to balance desirability, usability, viability, feasibility and delivery constraints
  • Advanced interaction and visual design skills, with close attention to detail, accessibility, consistency and usability
  • Strong systems thinking, including an understanding of how design decisions affect connected journeys, platforms, teams and future product development
  • Advanced proficiency in Figma, prototyping and component-based workflows, with experience contributing to or evolving design systems
  • Confidence choosing and applying appropriate research and validation methods rather than relying on a single process for every problem
  • Experience using qualitative and quantitative evidence to make decisions and evaluate outcomes
  • Practical familiarity with AI-assisted design workflows or clear evidence of actively developing this capability across areas such as ideation, research synthesis, content, prototyping, analytics or design review
  • The ability to assess AI output critically, recognise its limitations and use it responsibly rather than treating it as a replacement for customer insight or professional judgement
  • Strong communication, facilitation and storytelling skills, with the ability to explain decisions and influence stakeholders across disciplines and levels
  • A proactive approach to collaboration with Product and Engineering, including involving partners early and navigating constraints constructively
  • The ability to organise design artefacts and documentation so that decisions, specifications and context are easy for others to understand
  • The confidence to challenge assumptions, give and receive constructive feedback, and change direction when evidence calls for it
  • The ability to balance speed and quality, make pragmatic trade-offs and move work forward without waiting for perfect information
  • A user-first, low-ego approach grounded in curiosity, empathy, accountability and a strong sense of ownership
  • Fluent English language skills

And if you can also do this stuff, even better:

  • Experience designing fintech, payments, banking, SaaS or other complex and regulated digital products
  • Experience designing products for customers across different countries, languages, levels of financial literacy or accessibility needs
  • Experience working with complex data, experimentation platforms or product analytics tools
  • Familiarity with design tokens, Code Connect, code-backed prototyping or other workflows that help close the gap between design and implementation
  • Experience building or sharing AI-assisted workflows, prompt libraries, design-review practices or rapid prototyping approaches
  • Experience contributing to product strategy, roadmap conversations or cross-team initiatives beyond your immediate product area

What we believe

At TransferGo, we offer competitive rewards to all people. We know that recognition is about more than just money, and we’ve fostered a culture of kudos to shine a light on the great work throughout the business, and the people making it all happen. We hold regular in person events to connect with each other and help all our TransferNauts to grow with a generous training allowance. We believe that empowering people makes for a happier and more effective workforce. This means we enable anyone who wants to pursue initiatives that deliver real value for our migrant customers.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive Salary: Starting from 4,420 GBP - 5,530 GBP (gross) per month, depending on experience. Salary is just one part of the conversation – if you’re excited about the role but the range feels slightly off, don’t hesitate to apply. We’re open to discussing based on your experience and potential.
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Including a generous holiday allowance, competitive healthcare insurance, and a wellbeing package from day one.
  • Annual Development Budget: €1,000 to invest in your personal and professional growth.
  • Hybrid Working Environment: Flexibility to work from home and in the office, with most team members in the office two days a week.
  • Pet-Friendly Office: If you’re near one of our offices, bring your furry friend along!
  • Inclusive Culture: Regular in-person events, fostering a strong sense of community and collaboration.
  • Empowerment and Ownership: We believe in empowering our people to take initiative and drive meaningful change.

At TransferGo, we are committed to the equal treatment of all current and prospective employees. We will not tolerate discrimination on the basis of age, disability, sex, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race or ethnicity, religion or belief, gender identity,  marriage, civil partnership or any other protected category. We are proud of our diverse and inclusive culture and we strongly encourage suitably qualified applicants from a wide range of backgrounds to apply and join TransferGo. We look forward to meeting you!

Please note that all data collected will be handled in accordance with our candidates privacy policy (https://www.transfergo.com/privacy-policy/overview) and will only be used for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy. The data will be securely stored and deleted according to retention timeframe set in the candidates privacy policy. descriptionHtml:
PAUL macht Bestandsgebäude fit für eine klimaneutrale Zukunft. Dabei verbindest du Prozessanalyse, Softwareentwicklung, AI-Tools und Verantwortungsübernahme mit einer pragmatischen, ergebnisorientierten Arbeitsweise.

Klingt nach dir? Dann starte bei uns als

Senior Product Engineer (AI & Business Systems) (m/w/d) in Mannheim (Hybrid)

Deine Aufgaben

Geschäftsprozesse verstehen

  • Du analysierst End-to-End-Prozesse entlang unserer Wertschöpfungskette (Operations, Rollout, Service, Supply Chain, Finance, Customer Operations)

Software entwickeln

  • Du automatisierst Geschäftsprozesse mit modernen Software- und AI-Technologien und baust Integrationen zwischen bestehenden Systemen

Lösungen produktiv machen

  • Du übernimmst Verantwortung für deine Lösungen bis zum produktiven Einsatz
  • Du arbeitest eng mit Product, Engineering, Data und Operations zusammen
  • Du betreibst und verbesserst deine Lösungen kontinuierlich anhand von Nutzerfeedback und Kennzahlen

Technologie weiterentwickeln

  • Du bewertest neue Technologien, Frameworks und AI-Tools
  • Du treibst die technische Weiterentwicklung unserer Plattform aktiv mit voran
  • Du machst unsere Systemlandschaft einfacher, robuster und skalierbarer

Das bringst du mit

Fachlicher Hintergrund

  • Wichtiger als Ausbildung oder Studium ist uns, was du kannst und mitbringst — typische Wege in diese Rolle sind dennoch: ein Studium in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder eine vergleichbare technische Qualifikation, mit nachweisbarer Verantwortung für den produktiven Betrieb eigener Softwarelösungen
  • Du kommst z. B. aus Rollen wie Software Engineer, Technical Product Engineer, Platform Engineer oder aus Industrie-/Gebäudeautomation, Startup, Digitalisierung oder technischem Consulting
  • Du hast bereits komplexe Probleme gelöst und funktionierende Software über ihren gesamten Lebenszyklus begleitet

Erfahrung & Methoden

  • Erfahrung in der End-to-End-Entwicklung von MVPs, internen Tools und produktiven Anwendungen
  • Praxis in der Prozessanalyse entlang komplexer Wertschöpfungsketten sowie im Design von Systemintegrationen
  • Eigenständige, ergebnisorientierte Arbeitsweise mit sicherer Kommunikation gegenüber technischen und fachlichen Stakeholdern

Tools, Systeme & Sprache

  • Sehr gute Programmierkenntnisse, z. B. in Python, TypeScript oder Java
  • Erfahrung mit APIs, Datenbanken und Systemintegrationen sowie sicherer Umgang mit Git
  • Erfahrung mit AI-gestützter Softwareentwicklung (z. B. ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor oder vergleichbare Tools)
  • Von Vorteil: Erfahrung mit Cloud-Technologien

title: Senior Product Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

How we work

We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder, and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work.

We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods, usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart.

We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move.

Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest.

A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer.

The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 3, that looks like this:

 

What you'll be doing

  • Taking a customer problem from discovery to production inside a pod, getting close to customers yourself, framing the problem, and shipping in small increments guided by real customer signal rather than internal opinion.

  • Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced.

  • Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve.

  • Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting.

  • Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you.

  • Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating.

What you'll need to have done

  • Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered.

  • Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve.

  • Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps.

  • Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to.

  • Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce.

  • Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity.

  • Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them.

 

You’re unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

 

Compensation

At hx, we’re committed to salary transparency. You’ll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we’re working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

 

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

 

Interview process

  1. Initial chat with our Talent team

  2. Lead Hirer Interview

  3. Live AI Skills Assessment

  4. Values Interview with the CPTO

  5. Meet the CEO

 

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

 

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

title: Senior Product Engineer (Product Manager)
descriptionHtml:
About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

We're building a larger, dedicated Platform team at Lendable, increasing our investment in the infrastructure that enables our products and engineering teams to scale.

We're hiring a Technical Product Manager to sit within Engineering and connect platform technology, reliability and commercial value. You'll own what we prioritise and why, giving engineers the business context they need while helping Product and leadership understand the impact and opportunities that Platform enables.

This is a hands-on technical IC role, where you'll stay close to engineering through writing code, reviewing PRs and contributing to architecture discussions.

Working closely with the Platform Engineering Manager and Tech Lead, you'll help shape the Platform roadmap, connect technical investment to measurable business outcomes, and build the foundations that allow Lendable to move faster and scale with confidence.

What you'll be doing

Own platform stability

  • Own platform stability as a primary accountability - SLA/SLO metrics, incident rates, release quality.

  • Hold release gating authority: block features from production that don't meet testing standards or introduce unacceptable regression risk.

  • Enforce CI/CD standards centrally so pods don't fragment into one-off solutions.

  • Track and report stability metrics alongside commercial outcomes - stability is the foundation that makes the rest possible.

Be commercially accountable

  • Own the business case for platform investment and answer "why are we spending six engineers on this for three months?" in terms leadership understands.

  • Track platform impact in business terms: developer velocity, incident cost, time-to-market, reliability, capacity - e.g. "CXO rollout removes a 3-second API fan-out, reducing session abandonment" or "we can now handle 20k simultaneous logins".

  • Input into headcount and investment decisions for the platform team.

Own the platform roadmap

  • Own the platform backlog, prioritised by business value and sequenced to unblock the highest-value product teams first - not driven by technical debt or engineer preference alone.

  • Make trade-offs explicit: "if we do X now, we defer Y by Z weeks - here's what that means for products depending on us".

  • Ensure every initiative has a defined success metric that non-engineers can track.

Be the stakeholder interface

  • Act as the single point of contact for Pod Leads: business requirements coming from pods and engineering/developer requirements flowing to pods; prioritise both in service of platform stability.

  • Make platform work visible to leadership - regular forums with product MDs and PMs to capture upcoming dependencies before they become blockers; represent platform work in leadership reviews; translate technical milestones into business milestones.

  • Drive cross-team collaboration and buy-in with other PMs; engage architecture in technical design.

  • Escalate when product teams make requests that would create unsustainable platform load or technical debt.

Contribute as an engineer

  • Write code, review PR's, and participate in architecture design as a core part of the role - not a side project.

  • Bring a strong technical voice to roadmap decisions without owning final architecture calls (that's Architecture and Tech Leads).

What we're looking for

Essential

  • Deep, hands-on engineering background - this role must be staffed by someone who has shipped production systems, not someone who has only managed backlogs.

  • Strong commercial instinct: can build a business case, speak to P&L impact, and hold a line on ROI.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management across product, engineering, and finance without direct line authority over all of them.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity - platform value is often indirect and long-horizon.

  • Track record of contributing as an IC while operating at a senior, cross-team level.

  • Proactive, low-ego, and clear communicator - able to hold a line with leadership and pod leads alike.

Nice to have

  • Experience in platform, infrastructure, or developer tooling contexts.

  • Familiarity with SLA/SLO frameworks and incident management at scale.

  • Experience enforcing CI/CD standards across multiple teams or pods.

  • Prior work making "invisible" infrastructure legible to non-technical leadership.

Our tech stack

Platform & backend: Kotlin, AWS, Postgres, RabbitMQ, Docker, Kubernetes.

Gateway & clients: Node GraphQL gateway, React Native / TypeScript mobile app, Relay.

Tooling & observability: GitHub, GitHub Actions, Jira, Confluence, Datadog, Sentry, Grafana.

Interview process

  • Quick call with the Talent Team (30 minutes)

  • Hiring manager interview (30 minutes)

  • Technical and Product interview (90 minutes)

  • Culture-add interview (60 minutes)

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

  • Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover

  • Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans

  • Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members

  • Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations

  • Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations

Please note: The availability and details of specific benefits vary by location and role. For more information, please speak to your Talent Partner.

descriptionHtml:
About Motorway

Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.

This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to join Motorway's Product & Engineering team. Motorway is a UK online car-selling platform connecting private sellers with ~7,500 verified dealers through online auctions. You will own a problem area end to end, in either the seller or the dealer side of the marketplace, and be accountable for the outcomes you deliver.

Building is cheaper than it has ever been. The hard part now is choosing the right thing to build. We want PMs with exceptional product sense who find the problems worth solving, back that judgement with evidence, and use the latest technology to solve them in ways that weren't possible a year ago.

What you will do

Find the problems that matter

  • Identify the highest-impact problem areas by combining quantitative analysis with qualitative research, and explain clearly why they matter more than the alternatives

  • See through the hundreds of good ideas to the few that will move the business and create real value for sellers and dealers

  • Own outcome-based goals and metrics, not feature lists

Build with AI, in your work and in our product

  • Use AI to make yourself and your team faster: automate routine PM tasks, analyse data and research quickly, and prototype or vibe code solutions to get customer feedback in days, not weeks

  • Ask how each product could be built differently given what AI makes possible, and bring those ideas to your squad

  • Make your team 2x more effective, not 2x busier

Deliver with rigour

  • Lead a cross-functional squad of engineers, designers and data specialists from discovery through launch and measurement

  • Run experiments that produce learning even when they fail, and act on what you learn

  • Make clear trade-offs between customer needs, technical constraints and business priorities

Bring people with you

  • Communicate the what, the why and the how clearly, through crisp, data-led documents and conversations

  • Work with the people closest to you (engineering, design, data) and with execs and other business units such as Operations, Customer Support, Sales and Marketing

  • Influence without authority and build alignment on difficult decisions

Requirements

  • Proven experience as a product manager, with a track record of shipping products that moved meaningful business metrics, not just delivering features

  • Strong product sense. You can show how you found and prioritised the right problem, and what you chose not to do

  • Comfortable with both qualitative and quantitative evidence: you run user research and also query data, design experiments and interpret results yourself

  • Data-oriented. You use data to understand problems, set goals and measure impact, and can debate approaches with data scientists and analysts

  • AI-forward. You use AI tools regularly in your own work and have hands-on experience prototyping or building with them. You have a point of view on where AI helps and where it doesn't

  • A clear, confident communicator who can work with engineers and analysts day to day and with senior leaders across the business

  • Ability to move between detail and strategy without losing coherence

  • Self-starter with strong ownership, a curious mindset, and the ability to build domain knowledge quickly

  • Experience in marketplaces, consumer products or B2B platforms is helpful but not essential

  • You're excited about changing how people buy and sell cars

Benefits

We offer a fantastic range of benefits to help you thrive:

  • Hybrid work schedule with 2 days per week in our Central London office, with regular social events, office drinks and free snacks to keep you going

  • Great work-life balance

  • Stock options so you can share in Motorway's growth and future success

  • Pension scheme to plan for your future with our provider NEST

  • Strong commitment to your personal development including budget for books, courses, conferences, etc

  • Opt-in comprehensive health insurance through BUPA including dental care and fitness discounts

  • Cycle to work scheme, save big ££ on a new bike and accessories

  • One paid volunteering day a year for you to use as you wish

  • Generous parental benefits including 6 months full paid maternity leave, 4 weeks paternity leave and workplace nursery scheme... and much more!

title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
descriptionHtml:
Optics11 is a fast-growing high-tech company based in Amsterdam, developing advanced fiber optic sensing solutions for the most demanding environments. Our technology detects the earliest signs of failure in critical assets – from high-voltage energy infrastructure to subsea and defense applications – and gives our customers precise, real-time data they can act on.

As Senior Product Marketing Manager you will build a deep understanding of the end-to-end solutions (hardware and software) across all of Underwater Security (our OptiBarrier and OptiArray product lines and our software platform), and of the markets and customers they serve. You turn that understanding into clear positioning, compelling value propositions and go-to-market plans that help our sales teams win.

Optics11 is in its scale-up phase, and product marketing in Underwater Security is starting from a basic level. You will build the product marketing function from the ground up: you set up the frameworks, processes and tools it needs, while delivering tangible commercial results along the way. You start as an individual contributor, with the opportunity to grow a small product marketing team over time.

You will be part of the Product team in Underwater Security and work closely with our solutions Product Managers for hardware and software, Sales, Business Development, Marketing, Application Engineering, Customer Projects and R&D teams.

No two weeks will look the same. You might analyze a competitor’s new seabed monitoring system, sharpen the value proposition for an anti-submarine warfare (ASW) tender, work on the launch of a new software release, train the sales team on a new product narrative, or help prepare a customer demo for a tradeshow such as UDT or Euronaval. You will own how our products are positioned, launched and sold in the market, support pricing decisions, and make sure your market insights support Optics11 product decision making.

Within your first 6–12 months, you will have evolved the foundations of product marketing in Underwater Security: clearly defined target segments and buyer personas, a positioning and messaging framework per product line, a competitive intelligence baseline, a repeatable launch process and a first sales enablement toolkit. Your work will sharpen our market focus, improve our win rate and help Optics11 scale its solutions commercially in demanding, high-stakes markets.

Responsibilities:

  • Build the product marketing function by setting up the frameworks, processes, templates and tools for positioning, launches, competitive intelligence, sales enablement and product marketing analytics, tracking pipeline contribution and win rates, and scaling them as the organization grows.

  • Define target markets and commercialization plans by analyzing market size, trends, buying contexts and customer needs across mission profiles such as anti-submarine warfare (ASW), intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) and critical underwater infrastructure (CUI) protection, prioritizing segments and use cases with Product Management and Business Development, and defining go-to-market approaches, channels and partnerships per segment (e.g. with prime contractors and system integrators).

  • Lead competitive intelligence and market monitoring by tracking competitors, technologies, programs and tenders, running win/loss analyses, and sharing actionable insights with Product Management to shape strategy, roadmap and business cases.

  • Own product positioning, messaging and value propositions by developing clear, differentiated propositions per product line and segment, and translating technical capabilities into operational and commercial value for defense partners and clients.

  • Support Product Management on pricing and packaging by providing market, competitor and customer insights for pricing decisions on products and end-to-end solutions, and aligning price positioning with Sales.

  • Plan and execute product launches by introducing a launch process scaled to the size of each release, coordinating launch readiness across Product, Sales and Support, and providing product messaging, content and launch input to the Marketing team.

  • Enable sales and ensure commercial readiness by creating sales narratives, pitch decks, battlecards, objection handling and training, preparing customer demos, collateral and tender input with Tech Sales & Bid Management and Application Engineering, and supporting Sales, Business Development and Marketing in key opportunities, tenders and trade shows.


Requirements:

  • Master’s degree in marketing, business or engineering.

  • 5+ years of experience in product marketing for technical B2B or B2G solutions, preferably combining hardware and software (platform) products in defense or another industrial high-tech / high-compliance environment with long, complex sales cycles such as tenders and partner-led sales.

  • Proven experience building product marketing from the ground up in a scale-up: hands-on, pragmatic and entrepreneurial, setting up processes, frameworks and tools with limited resources while delivering results.

  • Demonstrable experience in defining value propositions, positioning and go-to-market plans, and executing them through launches and sales enablement.

  • Ability to quickly understand complex technology and translate it into clear, credible customer value.

  • Strong cross-functional leadership and stakeholder management skills at operational and management level.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English, capable of presenting to technical, commercial and executive audiences.

  • Proficiency in CRM and marketing automation tools such as HubSpot, and in analytics for funnel and performance reporting.

  • Willingness to travel, including to customers and international trade shows; driver’s license B (or international equivalent).

  • Ability to pass a background / security screening by the Dutch AIVD/MIVD, as you will be working with clients in the defense industry.

Nice to Have :

  • Experience in ASW, ISR or CUI-related defense technology markets, or with underwater acoustics, is a big plus.

  • Experience with defense procurement, tenders and export-controlled products.

  • Understanding of pricing and packaging for hardware, software and recurring-revenue (license or subscription) models.

  • Experience working with prime contractors and system integrators.

  • Proficiency in tools such as Jira Product Discovery, Confluence, Miro, PowerBI.

  • Proficiency in Dutch language is a plus

Screening

You will work with clients in the defense and security sectors. Obtaining a Certificate of No Objection issued by the AIVD, the Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service, is mandatory. This means you will need to undergo a security screening. We will explain the process and guide you through the applicable requirements.
